giuseppe montesi.name: Giuseppe Montesi
giuseppe montesi.origin: Monsignore Giuseppe Montesi was a powerful prelate who had been placed in charge of a little-known wing of the Vatican Library that was secretly devoted to occult lore. Like his ancestors stretching back eight centuries before him, Montesi was also the custodian of everything related to the Darkhold. When a learned priest named Father Ramón Jóquez died in California after having been possessed by the spirit of the evil monk Aelfric, those mysterious circumstances attracted considerable attention to his death. Father Jóquez's papers were sent to the Vatican Library where they were inspected by Montesi who discovered among them the notes that Jóquez had made while translating the true Darkhold for Jack Russell. Although incomplete, these notes were enough to enable Montesi to recreate the incantation from the Darkhold that could be used to destroy vampires, a spell that had long been known as the Montesi Formula. However, vampires who had been assigned to secretly keep watch over the prelate learned of this and informed their master, Count Dracula, that Montesi had obtained a copy of the Montesi Formula. The news caused Dracula to travel to Rome to deal with this threat. Montesi used the spell to destroy a number of recently-turned vampires while continuing research that he hoped would lead to him finding a way to destroy all vampires. One evening, while walking in Rome, Montesi came across an American tourist being attacked by a female vampire named Maria. After using his cross to force her away from her intended victim, Montesi then recited the spell, causing Maria to burst into flame and burn away to ashes. As he returned to the Vatican, Montesi heard a scream from above that he interpreted as being from a wounded bat. Correctly assuming that the source of that scream had been Dracula in bat form, Montesi chose to mock the vampire, saying that he had been expecting the count but was not quite ready to face him. Montesi then entered the Vatican, confident that no vampire could reach him there, and went to the Archives to continue his research. Not long afterwards, Montesi was taken completely by surprise when Dracula burst into the room and, before he could react, grabbed the paper containing the incantation from his hand and burned it in the flame of a nearby candle. When Montesi then fled from the room, Dracula initially let him go, intending to let the monk live so that he could spend the rest of his days reliving his defeat. However, only seconds later, Dracula realized that Montesi must have already memorized the spell and began to pursue him. Although weakened by all the crosses, Dracula eventually came to the Sistine Chapel where he found Montesi waiting for him. As the monk began reciting the spell, Dracula lunged at him, grabbing him around the throat to stop him from speaking, and then hurled him down at the floor with enough force to cause a lethal head injury. As Dracula laughed over him, the dying Montesi told the vampire that is was not over because he had, days earlier, mailed a copy of the incantation to Dracula's nemesis, Quincy Harker. As an enraged Dracula fled, other priests entered and found Montesi's dead body.

When Montesi then fled from the room, Dracula initially let him go, intending to let the monk live so that he could spend the rest of his days reliving his defeat. However, only seconds later, Dracula realized that Montesi must have already memorized the spell and began to pursue him. Although weakened by all the crosses, Dracula eventually came to the Sistine Chapel where he found Montesi waiting for him. As the monk began reciting the spell, Dracula lunged at him, grabbing him around the throat to stop him from speaking, and then hurled him down at the floor with enough force to cause a lethal head injury. As Dracula laughed over him, the dying Montesi told the vampire that is was not over because he had, days earlier, mailed a copy of the incantation to Dracula's nemesis, Quincy Harker. As an enraged Dracula fled, other priests entered and found Montesi's dead body.
powers: As a member of the Montesi family, Giuseppe Montesi was supposedly incorruptible and thus could not be influenced by the Darkhold.
equipment: Montesi Formula
fields.notes: In , the first story in which it appeared, the spell that Montesi used was not named and only referred to as the "Darkhold incantation." It was first called the Montesi Formula in in a story in which Elianne Turac had Quincy Harker kidnapped and interrogated in an attempt to get the spell from him. However, Harker insisted that he did not have the spell. In the story that introduced him, Montesi was simply an aged monk who had discovered a copy of the then-unnamed Darkhold incantation while doing research in the Vatican Library. It was only over a decade later, as part of a storyline in which the history of that spell was greatly expanded, that this character was given a first name and revealed to be a member of a family of priests who had been seeking to use the Darkhold to destroy vampires for centuries. Montesi was originally identified as being a monk but it was later revealed that he was actually a prelate, a high-ranking member of the Catholic Church, who only "affected the dress of a monk."

glaboo.name: Glaboo
glaboo.origin: Glaboo was a member of the Crimson Cadre were an elite military force created by the Inhuman Genetic Council following the self-exile of the Inhuman Royal Family to Earth. Under the command of General Ator, Glaboo was a member along with the flying Margoyle, the electrically powered Pulssus, the tree man known as Rootar, and the amphibious Eelak among others. The first recorded mobilization of the Crimson Cadre came when the Fantastic Four ventured to the moon to question the Watcher over his recent activities on Earth. General Ator demanded that the Fantastic Four be shot out of the sky due to their past assistance to the royal family in defying the Genetic Council. Although they lost track of the Fantastic Four's Stealth-Hawk ship, they were able to later track down the Thing later on the surface of the moon outside the Watcher's Citadel. They ambushed the thing and nearly overpowered him until they were forced by by Kristoff Vernard's retainer Boris who threatened to unleash the Stealth-Hawk's weapons upon them. Ator ordered his troops to retreat, but vowed to get revenge against the Fantastic Four. Not long after this, the Watcher's citadel was swallowed up in a vortex accidentally activated by Nathaniel Richards, which threatened to destroy the Inhumans home of Attilan. This coincided with the sorceress Morgan Le Fay raising the continent of Atlantis to the surface of Earth's oceans. Seeking to reclaim their ancestral home, the Genetic Council abandoned the Inhumans to their fate and went to Earth. Meanwhile, the Crimson Cadre discovered that a human was responsible and after arming themselves with an Atmo-Gun, traveled to Earth to get revenge against the human race, launching an attack in Florida. After the Cadre left Attilan, it was saved by the Fantastic Four, who shrunk it down to size and took it aboard their ship the Stealth-Hawk. The group were opposed by the members of Fantastic Force who were able to disable the Atmo Gun and trap the Crimson Cadre within a Negative Zone Barrier. While the Crimson Cadre were imprisoned, the Genetic Council formed and alliance with Morgan, recovered the shrunken city of Attilan and forced the royal family back into their service. The Crimson Cadre were later rescued by Karnak and were part of the defensive trying to stop the Fantastic Four, Fantastic Force, the Sub-Mariner and Thor from reclaiming Atlantis and Attilan. Ultimately, Attilan was restored to its normal size and contained under a Negative Zone Barrier. Trapped outside, the Crimson Cadre were ordered to apprehend the Inhuman Royal Family by the Genetic Council's ruler Lord Arcadius, but failed. Eventually, the Inhuman Royal Family came back into power, and while celebrating the return of Crystal, the Crimson Cadre was enthralled by Maximus and his ally Fabian Cortez who tried to take down the royal family. The Cadre's ranks were increased with the addition of the renegade Inhumans Leonus, Falcona, and Stallior. The Cadre was easily dispatched and later Maximus and Cortez were quickly defeated. The Cadre was easily dispatched and later Maximus and Cortez were quickly defeated. The Crimson Cadre has not been seen since, and has possibly been disbanded.

gladstone hawkins.name: Gladstone Hawkins
gladstone hawkins.origin: Doctor Gladstone Hawkins was a paleontologist who was requested by S.H.I.E.L.D. to join a special scientific task force known as the Godzilla Squad. As the name suggests, the team was charged with tracking down and confining the mutated dinosaur known as Godzilla. Hawkins accompanied S.H.I.E.L.D. agents Timothy "Dum Dum" Dugan and Gabe Jones as they tracked Godzilla throughout the New York area. It was Gladstone's suggestion that Godzilla would be more controllable if they could reduce him in size using Pym Particles. The tactic worked briefly, but Godzilla still managed to elude capture. Gladstone recommended herding Godzilla into the American Museum of Natural History where he was sure they could capture him so long as nobody violently provoked the creature. This stratagem also failed, due largely to interference by the Fantastic Four.

gladys fulton.origin: Gladys was a bartender from Liverpool who was ambushed and turned into a vampire by Dracula. One of her patrons, Corker Haller, went to check on her after hearing her scream, but he was then turned into another vampire by Gladys herself. Once both of them were outed as vampires, a townsfolk mob led by Father William, a local priest, chased and staked them both to death.

gladys smallwood.name: Gladys Smallwood
gladys smallwood.origin: Gladys Smallwood's husband, Tom, was captain of a fishing trawler. During a particularly bad storm, Tom was knocked overboard and sank, weighted by the sinkers on his fishing net. On the ocean floor he found a glowing egg, which, floating, pulled him to the top. He brought it home to his wife and grandson, Dan. Gladys saw that there was something inside the egg. She was sure it wasn't humanoid, but when she broke the shell she held a tiny infant female, yellow skinned and distinctly humanoid. Marrina, as she was named by the Smallwoods, grew up fast and eventually became a member of Alpha Flight. It was later revealed she was part of an alien race called the Plodex. They automatically adapt to any environment, and when Gladys broke the egg shell, she imprinted her with human female DNA.

glakandar.name: Glakandar
glakandar.origin: Glakandar was the first being appointed to be a Protector of the Universe by Eon and he was chosen five billion years ago. As member of the Stygian race, Glakandar was more commonly known as the Stygian Starbender. Although no details about his life and the circumstances of his death have been revealed, it is known that his usage of the Quantum-Bands caused some of his life essence to collect within them. Once Glakandar died, the residue of that life essence was transmitted to the White Room where it manifested as a spirit that animated a duplicate of his body that was made out of the substance of Eon's body. Apparently unaware of how he got there, this duplicate Stygian Starbender found himself sitting at a table in a room that seemed to be infinitely long, unable to move any part of his body except his head. As other Protectors of the Universe later appeared there, they discussed their theories about the White Room and agreed that it was the place where the spirits of all Protectors of the Universe went after they had served their times. While others believed that the White Room was either a place of eternal punishment or a purgatory where a final battle would someday occur, Glakandar believed it was Mokonris, a heaven where they were being rewarded for their days of valor. Billions of years later, after Eon herself had recently died, Thanos used the Infinity Gauntlet to create bio-duplicates of the Starbender and three other former wielders of the Quantum-Bands by tapping into Eon's vestigial memory and incarnating them in recreations of their original bodies made from the matter of Eon's body. Armed with fully-functional replicas of the Quantum-Bands, the foursome was sent to attack Quasar but he survived by killing the bio-duplicates of Glakandar, Trantra, and Ree and leaving the Marvel Boy bio-duplicate trapped in the Eonverse. Later, after Quasar himself had died and appeared in the White Room, Glakandar, who was sitting directly across from the newcomer, introduced himself by his name and his title, and revealed that they had met once, indicating that he somehow remembered what the Thanos-created bio-duplicate had experienced. Due to his possession of the Starbrand, Quasar was later able to leave the White Room.

glane.name: Glane
glane.origin: Thor tells Valkyrie and Nova about the young warrior Glane. Thor says Odin gave Glane a mission to send information about a troll army positions to a small company of Asgardian warriors. He failed because he lost the message while traveling through an enemy camp. Odin banished Glane to imprison his spirit in the underworld to perform tasks. Every year, either Valkyrie or Thor had to deliver Odin's message to Glane. Thor asks Nova accompanies to accompany himself and Valkyrie for delivering this year's message. The three heroes enter a portal to the Asgardian underworld battlegrounds. Thor tells Nova that their mission is also a trial for himself and Valkyrie because they also failed their missions when Glane failed his. A herd of goats attacks Glane, and Thor stops them. Later, they battle the neo-men. Nova starts to question whether Glane really deserved his punishment as they fight off Frost Giants. The three heroes reach the woods, and Thor carves a path for them to follow. They find Glane in the Cave of the Abyss. Thor shows Glane Odin's message saying he is forgiven. Nova and Valkyrie go back to Earth, and Thor stays in Asgard to fight the war with Glane.

glass.name: Glass
glass.origin: Glass was a mutant killer, who claimed to have killed a total of 68 people. He was hired as security for the shadowy organization of mutant businesspeople, the Gauntlet. When Helen Burnside led Nate Grey to the Gauntlet's headquarters with the mission of protecting them from the Down-Spiral creatures seeking to kill them, Glass stood in Grey's way and attacked him. He was easily defeated by the mutant shaman, who use his telepathic abilities to send Glass into a catatonic state.

glass girl.name: Glass Girl
glass girl.origin: ===Thanos' invasion=== Glass Girl was an Inhuman living in Attilan. When Attilan was evacuated during Thanos' invasion on Earth with the use of Eldrac, the Glass Girl was sent to Morocco, where she ended up being used by a group of thugs to make glass constructs to sell in bazaars in the region. ===New Attilan=== Months later, the head of New Attilan's Security Force, Frank McGee, tracked her down and retrieved Glass Girl from the village where she was being held. When McGee confronted her captors together with Naja and Flint, she created a lens with which McGee enhanced his optic light blasts and knocked out her captors. Glass Girl was then sent to New Attilan. ===Terrigen Conflict=== During the Terrigen Conflict, Glass Girl tried to escape from New Attilan together with Treste, Irelle, Ren Kimura, Sterilon, and a sixth unidentified Inhuman while their home was being held under siege by mutant forces. They were confronted by the Sleepers under Xorn's control, and Glass Girl was knocked down by a telepath. Once Archangel pacified the people in the scene, Glass Girl took care of the body of the unidentified Inhuman, who had been killed by Sebastian Shaw. At the end of the conflict, she joined the massive Inhuman party that retrieved Royal family members Maximus and Triton who were on the run and took down the Unspoken. ===Death of Inhumans=== When the Kree Imperium began ordering all surviving Inhumans to join it or perish, the empire launched an attack on the Inhuman city of New Arctilan on the Earth's Moon. During the attack, Glass Girl was one of the numerous Inhumans that were killed.

glazier.name: Glazier
glazier.origin: Glazier's origins are unknown, though she claimed not to have been born with her powers but to have acquired them after a man broke her heart. A white haired, white skinned woman who wore evening gloves to conceal her arms, she lived with her dog, Snowstar, in a house made of glass on a lonely stretch of beach, filled with what appeared to be glass statues of men. Finding Bruce Banner unconscious on the shore, she took him to her house and appeared to be tending to him out of kindness, until a month later Banner learned the truth: Glazier's evening gloves hid arms of crystal and her touch, under the light of a full moon, turned living things to glass, as she had done with all her male visitors before him. Glazier attempted to use her touch on banner, but he transformed into the Hulk and fought back, causing her to accidentally transform her faithful Snowstar into a statue which subsequently shattered. The Hulk's weight then caused the glass house to collapse, sending Glazier and himself plummeting into the sea. The Hulk escaped, but Glazier's own power had been turned on her when she touched herself with her uncovered arms in the confusion, and she was left as a glass statue standing on the sea bed.

glenda sandoval.name: Glenda Sandoval
glenda sandoval.origin: Glenda was a doctor who was married to Parnell Jacobs and was captured by some insurgents in the Kingdom of Aqiria in the middle of a civil war. This emergency forced his husband to help War Machine in his attempt to free the country and rescue Glenda. ===Payback time=== After a vicious battle, War Machine confronted Ares and Davis Harmon, Eaglestar's CEO and the man who kidnapped Glenda. Rhodey managed to defeat Ares, even for a brief moment and Harmon freed Sandoval from the confinement area. Harmon was sure that he couldn't be prosecuted by his war crimes due to the legal status of Aqiria, but that didn't stopped Glenda of taking justice into her own hands. But Harmon's deep secrets were opened by Ares, a rabid pack of prisoners infected by the ultimo virus. And Glenda was of the first victims becoming an enraged slave of the virus.

glenn reeper.name: Glenn Reeper
glenn reeper.origin: Glenn Reeper was a movie actor during World War II. He starred in the serial Adventures of Captain America, produced by Democracy Pictures. He met the real Captain America and Bucky who were guarding the movie set. During the shooting of a scene, Lyle Dekker sabotaged it and replaced the fake bullets for real ones and Glenn was shot, forcing the real Captain America to step in as his replacement.

glenn ryan.name: Glenn Ryan
glenn ryan.origin: Glenn Ryan was a 21 year old aspiring actor in Los Angeles who offered Daken a new drug called Heat at a party in Hollywood held by movie star Marcus Roston. Glenn and a young woman tried to seduce Daken, and Glenn offered Heat to spice up their tryst. Daken considered Glenn too shallow to maintain his interest, even though he did take the young man's pills. Glenn himself then, in the throes of drug-induced hallucinations, was chased and killed by someone he thought was a monstrous being.

glenn talbot.name: Glenn Talbot
glenn talbot.origin: Major Glenn Talbot was brought to Desert Base, New Mexico by its commanding officer, General Thaddeus E. "Thunderbolt" Ross, for two reasons. First, Ross wanted Talbot, who was the base's new security chief, to investigate nuclear physicist Dr. Bruce Banner, who had been working on various government projects at the base. Due to Banner's continuous and mysterious disappearances, Ross suspected not only that Banner was a traitor but also that he had some connection with the monstrous Hulk, who prowled the vicinity. Secondly, Ross objected to his daughter's love for Banner, whom Ross believed to be unmanly and contemptible even if he was not a traitor. Ross hoped that Betty would instead fall in love with Talbot, whom the general regarded as a fine example of a military man. Talbot, now General Ross's adjutant, continued to help Ross attempt to capture or destroy the Hulk, whom they regarded as a menace. At the time, Banner was unable to maintain his own intelligence and personality when he transformed into the Hulk. Eventually, though, he found a means by which his own persona could maintain control of the Hulk when he transformed into him. It appeared that the menace of the Hulk was over, and Ross reluctantly consented to the wedding of Banner and Betty. But the wedding ceremony was ruined when, just before Banner and Betty were officially joined in matrimony, the Hulk's archenemy, the Leader, returned Banner back to the Savage Hulk. Talbot swore to Betty that he would destroy the Hulk for this. Thinking that Banner was forever lost to her as a potential husband, Betty eventually married Glenn. Both Talbot and Ross believed that Betty actually still loved Banner, although Betty herself believed that she truly loved Talbot. Nevertheless, the two were correct. With the permission of the Canadian government, Ross and his Hulkbusters pursued the Hulk through Canada into the Arctic. Ross was taken prisoner by the Gremlin, who then headed a secret Soviet base that had been established there. The general was sent to a prison in the Soviet Union and Talbot volunteered to help rescue him. Although Ross was freed, Talbot himself was shot during the rescue mission and believed to be dead. Betty blamed her father for Talbot's reported demise. In reality, however, Talbot was still alive and being held prisoner by the Soviet at Bitterfrost, a top secret Soviet installation in Siberia. A man named Gregori Kronski was subjected to surgery that made him a double of Talbot. The Gremlin used his Psiclone device to imprint the memories and personality of Talbot in Kronski's mind, and those of Kronski's in Talbot's. Kronski was then sent to the United States, claiming to be an escaped Talbot. However, a bomb was concealed within Kronski's body. Gremlin's plan was to use the bomb to assassinate the President of the United States when the latter came to visit Gamma Base, where Talbot was stationed. Colonel Jack D. Armbruster saved the President's life, but both Armbruster and Kronski were killed when the bomb exploded. Ross then accompanied a team of S.H.I.E.L.D. agents led by Clay Quartermain into the Soviet Union to rescue the real Talbot. With assistance from the Hulk, Ross and Quartermain succeeded in freeing Talbot, who believed himself to be Kronski, and returned with them to the United States. There, Talbot's true personality and memories were restored. Talbot learned to his dismay that Betty no longer believed herself to be in love with him, and that she realized she had never stopped loving Banner. Glenn and Betty therefore soon received a divorce. The strain brought on by his many years of failures at ending the menace of the Hulk caused Ross to suffer a nervous breakdown(later revealed to be caused by Moonstone using her knowledge of psychology). He was relieved of command of Gamma Base, and Talbot, as the man with the next most experience battling the Hulk, was promoted to colonel and given command of Gamma Base by the Pentagon. Determined to gain vengeance for the loss of his wife's love and for Ross's nervous collapse, Talbot was intent on destroying the Hulk. Talbot though, proved no more successful at destroying the Hulk than Ross had been. Dissatisfied with Gamma Base's repeated failures to end the menace of the Hulk, Congress finally shut the base down. Now obsessed with killing the Hulk, Talbot committed treason by stealing the War-Wagon, a highly sophisticated flying battle cruiser, and went off on his own to locate and kill the Hulk. Talbot finally caught up with the Hulk at Mount Kuroishi, an inactive volcano, in Japan. Talbot launched a massive onslaught against the Hulk using the War-Wagon's immensely powerful arsenal of weaponry. The battle triggered an earthquake that reactivated the volcano. During the fight Talbot wore an encephalo-helmet that enabled him to take direct mental command of the War Wagon's controls (which ordinarily were run by on-board computers). thumb|left|300px|The demise of Colonel G

fields.base_of_operations: Gamma Base, New Mexico Formerly: Desert Base, New Mexico
fields.history: Major Glenn Talbot was brought to Desert Base, New Mexico by its commanding officer, General Thaddeus E. "Thunderbolt" Ross, for two reasons. First, Ross wanted Talbot, who was the base's new security chief, to investigate nuclear physicist Dr. Bruce Banner, who had been working on various government projects at the base. Due to Banner's continuous and mysterious disappearances, Ross suspected not only that Banner was a traitor but also that he had some connection with the monstrous Hulk, who prowled the vicinity. Secondly, Ross objected to his daughter's love for Banner, whom Ross believed to be unmanly and contemptible even if he was not a traitor. Ross hoped that Betty would instead fall in love with Talbot, whom the general regarded as a fine example of a military man. Talbot, now General Ross's adjutant, continued to help Ross attempt to capture or destroy the Hulk, whom they regarded as a menace. At the time, Banner was unable to maintain his own intelligence and personality when he transformed into the Hulk. Eventually, though, he found a means by which his own persona could maintain control of the Hulk when he transformed into him. It appeared that the menace of the Hulk was over, and Ross reluctantly consented to the wedding of Banner and Betty. But the wedding ceremony was ruined when, just before Banner and Betty were officially joined in matrimony, the Hulk's archenemy, the Leader, returned Banner back to the Savage Hulk. Talbot swore to Betty that he would destroy the Hulk for this. Thinking that Banner was forever lost to her as a potential husband, Betty eventually married Glenn. Both Talbot and Ross believed that Betty actually still loved Banner, although Betty herself believed that she truly loved Talbot. Nevertheless, the two were correct. With the permission of the Canadian government, Ross and his Hulkbusters pursued the Hulk through Canada into the Arctic. Ross was taken prisoner by the Gremlin, who then headed a secret Soviet base that had been established there. The general was sent to a prison in the Soviet Union and Talbot volunteered to help rescue him. Although Ross was freed, Talbot himself was shot during the rescue mission and believed to be dead. Betty blamed her father for Talbot's reported demise. In reality, however, Talbot was still alive and being held prisoner by the Soviet at Bitterfrost, a top secret Soviet installation in Siberia. A man named Gregori Kronski was subjected to surgery that made him a double of Talbot. The Gremlin used his Psiclone device to imprint the memories and personality of Talbot in Kronski's mind, and those of Kronski's in Talbot's. Kronski was then sent to the United States, claiming to be an escaped Talbot. However, a bomb was concealed within Kronski's body. Gremlin's plan was to use the bomb to assassinate the President of the United States when the latter came to visit Gamma Base, where Talbot was stationed. Colonel Jack D. Armbruster saved the President's life, but both Armbruster and Kronski were killed when the bomb exploded. Ross then accompanied a team of S.H.I.E.L.D. agents led by Clay Quartermain into the Soviet Union to rescue the real Talbot. With assistance from the Hulk, Ross and Quartermain succeeded in freeing Talbot, who believed himself to be Kronski, and returned with them to the United States. There, Talbot's true personality and memories were restored. Talbot learned to his dismay that Betty no longer believed herself to be in love with him, and that she realized she had never stopped loving Banner. Glenn and Betty therefore soon received a divorce. The strain brought on by his many years of failures at ending the menace of the Hulk caused Ross to suffer a nervous breakdown(later revealed to be caused by Moonstone using her knowledge of psychology). He was relieved of command of Gamma Base, and Talbot, as the man with the next most experience battling the Hulk, was promoted to colonel and given command of Gamma Base by the Pentagon. Determined to gain vengeance for the loss of his wife's love and for Ross's nervous collapse, Talbot was intent on destroying the Hulk. Talbot though, proved no more successful at destroying the Hulk than Ross had been. Dissatisfied with Gamma Base's repeated failures to end the menace of the Hulk, Congress finally shut the base down. Now obsessed with killing the Hulk, Talbot committed treason by stealing the War-Wagon, a highly sophisticated flying battle cruiser, and went off on his own to locate and kill the Hulk. Talbot finally caught up with the Hulk at Mount Kuroishi, an inactive volcano, in Japan. Talbot launched a massive onslaught against the Hulk using the War-Wagon's immensely powerful arsenal of weaponry. The battle triggered an earthquake that reactivated the volcano. During the fight Talbot wore an encephalo-helmet that enabled him to take direct mental command of the War Wagon's controls (which ordinarily were run by on-board computers). thumb|left|300px|The demise of Colonel G
equipment: Talbot has sometimes used the Mandroid Armor, the War-Wagon and other SHIELD equipment against the Hulk.
fields.trivia: Cable first mistook Red Hulk for Glenn Talbot instead of Thaddeus Ross, suggesting that Talbot became a Hulk at some point in Cable's future.

gletkin.name: Gletkin
gletkin.first_appearance: Iron Man: The Animated Series Season 1 1
gletkin.origin: Gletkin was a Russian sailor stationed on the submarine Prometheus. While the Prometheus was traveling undersea off the coast of Norway, an armed Gletkin accompanied Captain Karkov while tracking signs of an intruder to a cargo hold. After opening the hatch and stepping inside, they encountered the costumed villain Hypnotia assembling a bio-conversion device. When Gletkin ordered her to raise her hands, Hypnotia turned to face the two sailors, then paralyzed them with her hypnotic powers. After Hypnotia escaped the vessel by laser-cutting through the hull and flooding it, Gletkin and the captain were cocooned in a strange fluid. One year later, the Mandarin remotely activated the device planted on board the Prometheus, awakening Gletkin and the rest of the crew from their suspended animation, now transformed into subservient "radioactive zombie" warriors. The zombie Gletkin and crew then attacked and entered the undersea Hammer Channel Tunnel, exiting at the London terminal during its opening ceremony. Their attempts to contaminate the population with radioactivity were halted by Iron Man and Force Works, after which the sailors were transformed back to their normal human selves.

glider man.name: Glider-Man
glider man.origin: Glider-Man's Uncle Glen was murdered by Ben Parker, leading him to pursue updraft-based justice but he was prevented from killing Uncle Ben by Slider-Man who revealed that Uncle Glen had been hired to kill Slider-Man's Uncle Sven. The two were interrupted by Health Care Provider-Man, who revealed that Uncle Sven had killed Health Care Provider-Man's Uncle Ken. Albert Camus's "The Outsider"-Man appeared soon after, revealing that Uncle Ken was about to murder Albert Camus's "The Outsider"-Man's Uncle Den. Large Hadron Supercollider-Man, Ring-Binder Divider-Man, Zack Snyder-Man, Tidier-Man, Wider-Man, and Ghost-Rider Man also turned up in and around the house.

glindlefit.name: Glindlefit
glindlefit.origin: Glindlefit was one of several dwarves who escaped from the mines of Nidavellir and settled in Los Angeles. The Dwarves' plan was to use the magical ore of a meteor they stole from a Viking museum exhibit to possess the body of a mindless Norse monster, and take over Los Angeles for wealth and power. Glindlefit was to be sacrificed, so his soul could be transferred into the ore, and subsequently into the monster. Before they could begin the ceremony to transfer Glindlefit's soul into the ore, Ghost Rider appeared, in order to avenge the death of a port operator they killed as part of their plan. Hawkeye joined the brawl, having investigated the theft of the meteor at the request of the museum's curator. Gwenpool also stepped in, having been unintentionally teleported inside Ghost Rider's trunk. In the middle of the confusion caused by Gwenpool's appearance, Glindlefit and the rest of the dwarves escaped without the ore. Glindlefit and the dwarves then moved to the Port of Los Angeles, awaiting a shipment crate containing the mindless beast, as well as one of their own that had the task of recovering the ore. Having joined forces, Gwenpool, Hawkeye and Ghost Rider intrevened in the dwarves' plan once again. Gwenpool managed to retrieve the ore, which had become possessed by her ghost friend Cecil, and incrusted it into the mindless beast. Now in control of the monster, Cecil threatened the dwarves into fleeing back to Nivadellir.

glitch.name: Glitch
glitch.first_appearance: Iron Man: Kiss and Kill Vol 1 1
glitch.origin: Due to amnesia, Glitch only remembers the past year or so of her life. During that time, she has worked as a freelance thief. Although not many details were given, Glitch had helped Wolverine in the past, resulting in him owing her a favor. Glitch worked for Sebastian Shaw in exchange for information on her family, stealing a prototype from a Stark Industries lab. However, instead of providing her with this information, Shaw claimed that she had to do more work. In the end, she stole the information he had on her family, and gave both Shaw's and Stark's prototype to Iron Man. She then left to go seek her family out.

glitternight.name: Glitternight
glitternight.origin: Glitternight was once counted among the powerful cosmic entities known as the Five-Who-Are-All, dwelling in the Region Beyond Reality. He turned on his fellow entities, absorbing the being called Fire-Eyes. In response, Cowled One, Goat-Child, and Burning Snake banded together to defeat him. Stripped of much of his power and reduced to a smaller form, Glitternight was cast out of their realm and found his way to Earth, bringing with him strange, soul-affecting powers. On Earth, he became a formidable sorcerer and instructed Taboo in forbidden magical arts. Following Taboo’s death, Glitternight summoned his spirit, hoping to win him as an ally. However, when Glitternight revealed a plan to exterminate humanity and turn their souls into a demonic legion, Taboo turned against him. Meanwhile, Topaz sought Glitternight's help in restoring her declining mystical powers. Instead, he stole part of her soul and used it to create a monstrous Soul-Beast that appeared in California. The creature was eventually destroyed by Jack Russell, who had taken on his Werewolf form. Soon after, Glitternight confronted Jack and his companions—Topaz, Lissa Russell, and Buck Cowan—at Jack’s ancestral home on Blackgar Island. The timing coincided with Lissa’s first transformation into a werewolf. Glitternight tampered with her change, turning her into a monstrous Were-Demon under his control. Taboo, using the last of his mystical essence, merged with Lissa to free her from Glitternight’s influence. This act also lifted her family’s werewolf curse. The Werewolf attacked Glitternight and shattered the soul-emblem on his chest, triggering an explosion that appeared to destroy him. Though believed dead, Glitternight survived and resurfaced in Haiti, where he took command of an army of zombies and warped Topaz into a Harpy-like creature. He used both as part of a plan to harvest humanity’s collective soul. When the remaining Three-Who-Are-All intervened, they guided Jack Russell and Brother Voodoo to oppose him. During their battle, Glitternight called upon Fire-Eyes once more. Brother Voodoo severed their bond, prompting Fire-Eyes to turn on Glitternight, resulting in what seemed to be the destruction of them both. The event also enhanced Jack’s control over his lycanthropic transformations.

glomm.name: Glomm
glomm.origin: Glomm was a Deviant warrior who, at an unspecified point prior to or during the wider conflict involving Kang the Conqueror’s war on Earth, broke from Deviant authority structures and entered service under Dulpus, becoming one of his trusted combat assets and ultimately his designated champion. During a conflict in an underground Deviant stronghold, a group of Avengers were surrounded by overwhelming numbers of Deviant forces. In accordance with internal Deviant combat customs, leadership was contested through formalized single combat. Dulpus selected Glomm to represent him in the confrontation against Warbird. In the ensuing battle, Glomm engaged Warbird using his ability to engulf opponents within his own body mass, placing her in immediate physiological danger. Warbird managed to exploit a vulnerability within Glomm’s internal structure, striking a critical point that caused his defeat and physical collapse. As a result of the outcome, Warbird assumed control over the assembled Deviant forces and ordered their surrender. At a later stage of the wider war against Kang’s occupation forces, Deviant units—now operating in coordination following prior negotiations—participated in coordinated assaults against Kang’s army in Japan. Glomm was present among these Deviant combatants during the engagement against Kang’s forces, contributing to the overall offensive action that helped push them back.

During a conflict in an underground Deviant stronghold, a group of Avengers were surrounded by overwhelming numbers of Deviant forces. In accordance with internal Deviant combat customs, leadership was contested through formalized single combat. Dulpus selected Glomm to represent him in the confrontation against Warbird. In the ensuing battle, Glomm engaged Warbird using his ability to engulf opponents within his own body mass, placing her in immediate physiological danger. Warbird managed to exploit a vulnerability within Glomm’s internal structure, striking a critical point that caused his defeat and physical collapse. As a result of the outcome, Warbird assumed control over the assembled Deviant forces and ordered their surrender. At a later stage of the wider war against Kang’s occupation forces, Deviant units—now operating in coordination following prior negotiations—participated in coordinated assaults against Kang’s army in Japan. Glomm was present among these Deviant combatants during the engagement against Kang’s forces, contributing to the overall offensive action that helped push them back.

glop statue.name: Glop (Statue)
glop statue.origin: ===Overview=== Glop was a giant statue which came to life due to mystical paint. ===Origin=== A painter takes a job from a mysterious old man who wants him to paint a statue in a castle located in Transylvania. He tells the painter to leave the castle before midnight, but the painter is knocked unconscious by falling masonry as he is leaving and awakes just before midnight. The Glob comes to life and attempts to destroy the painter, but the man successfully eludes him. The old man returns to him and questions why he did not leave the castle as instructed. Then he reveals himself to be a scientist who had discovered the statue besides the strange paint cans with a note that claimed the statue was an alien advance scout for an invasion that could be activated by applying the paint and waiting until midnight which is why he hired the painter to see if it was true. The painter defeats the Glob with a can of turpentine. Years later he was among a group monsters on Monster Isle that the Infinity Watch encountered after their ship crash landed on Earth.

gloria angel.name: Gloria Angel
gloria angel.species: Human mutated by ionic energy, depowered
gloria angel.origin: ===Early Life=== Gloria Angel was once a popular actress in Hollywood, known for her roles in classic films. After retiring from acting, she took over as manager of a Los Angeles apartment building that became home to a diverse and creative group of residents. Among her tenants were aspiring actor Simon Williams, also known as Wonder Man, and other entertainment industry hopefuls such as Argus LaVecchio, LaHoya Scripps, and Aundray Phelps. Despite her retired status, Gloria remained actively involved in the lives of her tenants. She provided maternal guidance and emotional support, especially as the group became entangled in the unusual events surrounding Wonder Man's volatile ionic energy. ===Transformation by Ionic Energy=== After Wonder Man was assaulted by Angkor, the residents carried him home, only to witness a sudden and violent discharge of unstable ionic energy. Though initially showing no signs of injury, all eight individuals present Gloria included later developed superhuman abilities as a result of their exposure. Gloria discovered she had gained the ability to travel through time, allowing her to momentarily enter temporal anomalies or shift across moments in history. Despite her age and retired lifestyle, Gloria accepted this transformation with grace and purpose. ===Founding the Crazy Eight=== When the group decided to form a superhero team in response to Wonder Man's increasing instability, Gloria chose to join them, taking the name Glamour Girl a nod to both her Hollywood past and her newly acquired powers. As the Crazy Eight, the group included Gloria, Auteur, Dreamer, Stat, Snap, Buff, Visionary, and Attractive Lad. Gloria's time abilities were used strategically, providing the team with glimpses into alternate outcomes or warning them of imminent threats. Their first major battle was against Armed Response, a corrupt private enforcement unit linked to crime boss Lotus Newmark. After exposing the operation, the team was targeted by assassins Splice and Rampage. Gloria participated in the defence of her friends, although her powers were more subtle and less combative than others. ===Aftermath=== Eventually, Wonder Man reabsorbed the ionic energy from his allies to stabilise himself, removing Gloria's powers in the process. She returned to a more ordinary life but continued to serve as an anchor for the group, especially after Wonder Man's apparent death. In the aftermath, Gloria legally adopted or became the guardian of Esteban.

gloria brickman.name: Gloria Brickman
gloria brickman.origin: Gloria Brickman, the daughter of Senator Ralph Brickman and step-daughter of Mallory Brickman. Little does Gloria know, Mallory is none other than the shape-shifting mutant Mystique, operating undercover. After her mission was complete she faked her disappearance. Gloria encountered Mystique again in her quest for vengeance against Sabretooth. She reverted to a former persona of Mallory Brickman. Craftily engineering her reappearance as Mallory, who had supposedly been abducted, Mystique ensured federal agents found her bound in a car trunk, alleging captivity by Sabretooth. Though her husband welcomed her return eagerly, Gloria grew suspicious, attempting to involve an FBI agent. Mystique deflected this threat by insinuating the agent's misconduct, leading to his reassignment. Under the guise of Mallory, Mystique had her tracking implant removed by the family doctor, citing Sabretooth's coercion, but fearing exposure, she later silenced him by tampering with his car brakes. Mystique later killed her father to replace him.

gloria dayne.name: Gloria Dayne
gloria dayne.origin: Fontanelle was born in 1950. Her mother was the woman known as the Black Womb. Fontanelle remembered her mother aging, but at a slower rate than other humans. Fontanelle's mental powers manifested at some point before her 20s, and she has suffered from a perpetual headache since the powers emerged. Fontanelle's mother disappeared by the time Fontanelle herself was in her early 20s. Fontanelle assumed that her mother had died. Left to fend for herself, Fontanelle earned a decent living as a dream therapist. Her powers allowed her to access the minds of other people through their dreams. While building her respectable career as a therapist, she had a secret life as part of a bondage and domination "clinic." The Courier arrived at Fontanelle's "clinic" with an offer of emloyement for her. His boss the New Son wanted the dream therapist to work on a psychological profile of the mutant thief Gambit. Fontanelle accepted the offer. She did not meet her new employer in person, and she was unaware that the New Son was an alternate-reality version of Gambit. Fontanelle was initially unable to enter Gambit's mind, so she decided to study the memories of people who knew him well. She started entering the minds of the X-Men, but she only got giimpses at what they remembered about Gambit. Professor X had trained the team to resist deeper mental probes. Most of them felt guilty that they had abandoned Gambit alone in Antarctica. From Storm's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a devilish charmer, with no real regrets in life. From Iceman's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a pitiful figure, the thief's cool persona barely able to hide his deep sadness. From Beast's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a bipolar figure, sadness and callousness contrasting with intelligence and moral restraint in the same person. From Sabretooth's mind, she learned that he viewed Gambit as a figure that had earned both his respect and his resentment. From Frenzy's mind, Fontanelle learned that the young woman had mixed feelings of love and hate for Gambit. From the minds of most of the Marauders, she felt that they all respected Gambit. To Fontanelle's surprise, her mental probings also produced images of her own mother. Figuring that she shared a destiny with Gambit (as implied in the dreamscape), Fontanelle started investigating for personal reasons. Fontanelle entered the dreams of Jean-Luc LeBeau and discussed with him about aspects of his son's early life. Why he chose to keep Gambit away from the Antiquary and his schemes, why he chose others to train his son while he watched from a safe distance, and whether Gambit's engagement to Bella Donna Boudreaux was motivated by love or political machinations. Fontanelle learned a lot from the conversation, but openly questioned whether aspects of Gambit's life story were accidents of fate or parts of a hidden agenda. Fontanelle questioned the Courier, asking him about the New Son's reaction to Gambit preventing him from obtaining Garbha-Hsien's hidden technology. The Courier changed the topic, inforning Fontanelle that Gambit was already on a mission to steal something from the X-Men. Fontanelle entered Tante Mattie's dreams, observing Mattie as a young woman being threatened with death by an angy mob. In the dream, Gambit arrived and rescued the damsel-in-distress. With the events of the dream happening long before Gambit's supposed birth, Fontanelle wondered whether Gambit was a time-traveler. She also wondered whether the seemimgly young thief is much older than previously thought. Fontanelle entered Sekmeht Conoway's dreams, and witnessed how Gambit rescued Sekmeht from an accidental death, shortly following the girl's chance encounter with Ozymandias. Fontanelle considered Sekmeht's memories undreliable, but she noted that Sekmeht dreamed about Gambit kissing her after the rescue. Fontanelle entered the dreams of Carter Ryking in search for information about her own mother. She learned that both Carter and Charles Xavier had encounters with the Black Womb in their youth. Fontanelle tried entering the dreams of the New Son, and she wondered why images from his memories seemed familiar to her. The New Son confronted her in the dreamscape and kicked her out. At a later point, Fontanelle considered that the New Son had "memories" belonging to someone else. Fontanelle entered the dreams of Kim Purcell. She was the sister of Mary Purcell, the disembodied spirit which was bonded to Gambit for a time. Fontanelle needed information on Mary. Fontanelle entered the dreams of the Scalphunter in order get infornation on Gambit's role in the Mutant Massacre. She reported to the New Son that Gambit was a victim of his own stupidity, and that he had not actually murdered anyone during the Massacre. Fontanelle confronted Gambit in his own dreams, introducing herself as his dream guide. She playfully told the younger mutant that she would like to see him stripped to

fields.history: Fontanelle was born in 1950. Her mother was the woman known as the Black Womb. Fontanelle remembered her mother aging, but at a slower rate than other humans. Fontanelle's mental powers manifested at some point before her 20s, and she has suffered from a perpetual headache since the powers emerged. Fontanelle's mother disappeared by the time Fontanelle herself was in her early 20s. Fontanelle assumed that her mother had died. Left to fend for herself, Fontanelle earned a decent living as a dream therapist. Her powers allowed her to access the minds of other people through their dreams. While building her respectable career as a therapist, she had a secret life as part of a bondage and domination "clinic." The Courier arrived at Fontanelle's "clinic" with an offer of emloyement for her. His boss the New Son wanted the dream therapist to work on a psychological profile of the mutant thief Gambit. Fontanelle accepted the offer. She did not meet her new employer in person, and she was unaware that the New Son was an alternate-reality version of Gambit. Fontanelle was initially unable to enter Gambit's mind, so she decided to study the memories of people who knew him well. She started entering the minds of the X-Men, but she only got giimpses at what they remembered about Gambit. Professor X had trained the team to resist deeper mental probes. Most of them felt guilty that they had abandoned Gambit alone in Antarctica. From Storm's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a devilish charmer, with no real regrets in life. From Iceman's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a pitiful figure, the thief's cool persona barely able to hide his deep sadness. From Beast's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a bipolar figure, sadness and callousness contrasting with intelligence and moral restraint in the same person. From Sabretooth's mind, she learned that he viewed Gambit as a figure that had earned both his respect and his resentment. From Frenzy's mind, Fontanelle learned that the young woman had mixed feelings of love and hate for Gambit. From the minds of most of the Marauders, she felt that they all respected Gambit. To Fontanelle's surprise, her mental probings also produced images of her own mother. Figuring that she shared a destiny with Gambit (as implied in the dreamscape), Fontanelle started investigating for personal reasons. Fontanelle entered the dreams of Jean-Luc LeBeau and discussed with him about aspects of his son's early life. Why he chose to keep Gambit away from the Antiquary and his schemes, why he chose others to train his son while he watched from a safe distance, and whether Gambit's engagement to Bella Donna Boudreaux was motivated by love or political machinations. Fontanelle learned a lot from the conversation, but openly questioned whether aspects of Gambit's life story were accidents of fate or parts of a hidden agenda. Fontanelle questioned the Courier, asking him about the New Son's reaction to Gambit preventing him from obtaining Garbha-Hsien's hidden technology. The Courier changed the topic, inforning Fontanelle that Gambit was already on a mission to steal something from the X-Men. Fontanelle entered Tante Mattie's dreams, observing Mattie as a young woman being threatened with death by an angy mob. In the dream, Gambit arrived and rescued the damsel-in-distress. With the events of the dream happening long before Gambit's supposed birth, Fontanelle wondered whether Gambit was a time-traveler. She also wondered whether the seemimgly young thief is much older than previously thought. fields.notes: Fontanelle was part of a storyline which frequently hinted that Gambit was created by the Black Womb Project, as a byproduct of the expreriments of Dr. Nathan Milbury and Amanda Müeller. The storyline ended abruptly, without confirming any of the informatiin provided in these issues. The suggestion has been mostly ignored in subsequent stories. Fontanelle feels relatively relaxed or safe within the dreamscapes of relatively sane individuals, such as Sabretooth, Scalphunter , and Bullseye . For some reason, she found the dreamscape of Mister Sinister to be rather scary or disturbing, forcing her to flee. It is not entirely clear what she viewed in there.
fields.trivia: "Fontanelle" is an anatomical term for the soft membranous gaps (sutures) in the cranial bones of human infants. Fontanelles allow the infant brain to be imaged through using ultrasonography. Once they are closed, most of the brain is inaccessible to ultrasound imaging, because the bony skull presents an acoustic barrier. Fontanelle's typically blonde hair is depicted as green hair in several images. Since these are part of the encounters which she has in the dreamscapes of several characters, whether this change in color is part of a mental illusion or whether it reflects her actual appearance is unclear.

gloria garsen.name: Gloria Garsen
gloria garsen.origin: Glory was once Edwin Jarvis' girlfriend. She knew Jarvis while she was travelling in New York City subway and he helped her and other passengers for problems related to Inferno. After being helped, Glory decided to follow Jarvis so that he doesn't get away from her, and after getting saved once again from getting crushed by two cars and from a giant robot she declared her interest to Edwin, who accepted to take her back home. After that they started dating.

gloria grant.name: Gloria Grant
gloria grant.origin: Gloria Grant was seen for the first time when she met Peter Parker and Flash Thompson. Parker had moved into a new apartment, and she was living down the hall. On seeing his camera she told him that fate had brought them together as she was a model and he a photographer. Soon after she met Mary Jane Watson, who had just returned from the hospital, and invited Peter to a party at her apartment. Gloria then became a secretary for J. Jonah Jameson at the Daily Bugle when his original secretary, Betty Brant, left and he could not find anyone to replace her. Later, she got involved with the werewolf criminals the Lobo Brothers, and fell in love with Eduardo Lobo. During the gang war between Wilson Fisk and the Lobo Brothers, while shooting to kill Spider-Man, she accidentally killed Eduardo. She was later seen dating Randy Robertson, son of former Daily Bugle Editor Joe Robertson. Later, Glory was seen dating a young man named Lewis. When Jameson becomes mayor of New York City, Grant became one of his aides, appearing with him at the Raft on the day of Alistaire Smythe's execution. However, she later quit his administration when she saw that Jameson would never end his personal vendetta against Spider-Man. Glory started working from Daily Bugle as Senior National Desk Editor.

gloria grimly.name: Gloria Grimly
gloria grimly.origin: Gloria Grimly is the daughter of Joshua Grimly. She recently left the congregation led by his father and would go on to stay with Ron Williamson. While she continued to stay with Ron, Gloria would later visit her father at the church and offered money to him. However, Joshua refused the money. Shortly after, she met Williamson, who revealed his plan about blackmailing the City Hall. Seeing how cruel he was, she tried to flee from him, only for Ron to send two henchmen in trying to kidnap her, but Ghost Rider arrived and stopped them.

gloria jenkins.name: Gloria Jenkins
gloria jenkins.origin: Gloria Jenkins was a night club cigarette girl and was the granddaughter of Ezra Jenkins, the master engraver of the Department of Engraving in Washington, D.C.. With a subterfuge Ezra was captured together with his granddaughter by a gang of Nazis led by Peter Stromboli and was forced to engrave on an original 1000 dollar bill matrix so that Stromboli could print the banknotes and put them on the market in order to collapse the American economic system. The plot of Stromboli was however opposed by the intervention of Captain America and Bucky who defeated and captured Stromboli and his gang and freed Gloria and her grandfather.

gloria mayes.name: Gloria Mayes
gloria mayes.origin: Gloria Mayes worked as a police detective in a town in Arizona. She investigated a robbery at a gas station that resulted in the deaths of Sandy Brockhurst, Josh Alfaro, and Bruce Banner, though the latter was not identified. At night, the unidentified corpse had disappeared from the morgue, leaving a wall torn down. The perpetrator, Tommy Hill, appeared severely beaten up in the parking lot of a hospital and witnesses from the Dogs of Hell claimed they had been attacked by someone big and green. This led Detective Mayes to suspect the attacker had been the Hulk, and that the unidentified victim had been Bruce Banner even though at the time Banner was believed dead.

gloria munoz.name: Gloria Muñoz
gloria munoz.origin: ===Origin=== After her Cuban father and Seminole mother divorced when she was twelve, Gloria Muñoz moved out with her mother and lived with her until she was 16. Having discovered her mutant powers, she left to live on her own and spent some time in Miami. During this time, Sledge helped her out of some trouble, and she promised to aid him in the future, a favor which was eventually repaid when she was tasked with bringing him the mutant Warpath. ===Adventures with Warpath=== Luring Warpath to a meeting with an urgent message, Risque exploded a car near him to get his attention, and he threw a car at her in retaliation, which Risque imploded. She kissed Warpath and then fled, leaving a mysterious first impression. When Warpath was injured in a battle with Selene of the Externals, Risque pulled him away and took him to Florida, where she helped him recuperate and convinced him to stay with her, not even calling his team X-Force, to tell them where he was. The two became romantically involved and spent days mostly relaxing, though they also prevented the anti-mutant Friends of Humanity from harming a burn victim the group thought was a mutant. 180px|thumb|left|With James When Warpath heard reports of disaster striking New York City, he led Risque back to the X-Mansion, where they found Mister Sinister fighting X-Force and joined in battle against him. Unfortunately, they were all knocked out as Nate Grey launched a powerful psychic attack against Sinister that was reflected on X-Force. While they were all still unconscious, Sledge's mutant servants Blob and Mimic pulled Risque out, leaving Warpath wondering what had happened to her. Sledge reminded Risque of their deal so she met with him again and took him to a nightclub, where they were attacked by Blob and Mimic. They managed to defeat the duo, but Risque realized she could no longer stall and sedated Warpath with a drugged drink and delivered him to Sledge. Seeking to lay low, Risque then went to Wackyworld, a theme park she loved as a child, but X-Force tracked her there. She evaded them, even using her power to collapse a wall on Caliban, X-Force's monstrous mutant tracker, but when Caliban suffered a nervous system attack, Risque slowed to help him and was captured. X-Force made her take them to Sledge and Warpath, but once they got there the two had already discussed everything, and Warpath was ready to go back to his team. Before leaving, he told Risque he felt betrayed and didn't want to see her again. Later, Risque teamed with the Vanisher to steal the Heart of Pele, a sacred jewel in Hawaii. The Hawaiian goddess Pele found her and took her form, leaving her in an enchanted sleep on the beach, while she teamed up with X-Force, and fought the Lava Men. When the ethereal Demon Bear rampaged through one of Sledge's holdings, Risque was sent to aid X-Force in stopping it. Risque was reunited with Warpath and the two were briefly transported to an alternate dimension where they battled an alternate Danielle Moonstar, and helped defeat the Bear. ===After Warpath=== Risque joined the X-Corporation, set up by Charles Xavier to protect the rights of mutants internationally, and was based in Hong Kong with Domino, another former X-Force member. Within a few weeks, Risque learned of mutants being killed for body parts to be transplanted into regular humans and decided to investigate, but was murdered by John Sublime's U-Men. Risque, along with many other deceased mutants, was resurrected by Selene and Eli Bard with the Transmode Virus. During this time, she met James once more, but was presumably returned to the after-life after Selene's defeat. ===S.W.O.R.D.=== Risque returned to life, presumably revived by The Five, and became a citizen of Krakoa. She then joined S.W.O.R.D.'s mutant sub-team The Six, under the command of Abigail Brand.

gloria roza.name: Gloria Roza
gloria roza.origin: Gloria Roza's father was a respected Venezuelan police officer, who was killed when she was twelve. To honor him, Gloria followed a similar career, and later in her life became a United Nations Security officer. Her mind was invaded by Elisa Warsame, a psychologist whose family was killed by the military forces of the current president of Akima, Aliman Lor. Lor was set to address the United Nations, and Warsame wanted him dead in revenge. Roza agreed to follow Warsame's commands, and was prepared to shoot Lor when he was entering the building. However, Warsame's former patient Marc Spector intervened and saved Lor's life at the cost of being blamed for an attempted attack. Spector's intervention snapped Roza out of Warsame's control.

gloria santiago.name: Gloria Santiago
gloria santiago.origin: Gloria grew up very close to her sister, Rachel, until she began working as a housekeeper at the Marquis Hotel and secretly sleeping with movie star Jack Vaughn. Believing Rachel to be under control of an "evil mutant", Gloria hired X-Factor Investigations to find out the truth. Urged to investigate by Layla Miller, Siryn agreed to take the case. Siryn was able to get pictures of Rachel and Vaughn together, and reported the news to a shocked Gloria. Vaughn and Rachel were participating in a consensual and casual relationship, but Vaughn liked to play out rape fantasies and even used a loaded gun as a prop. When Gloria barged in to confront the two, the gun went off and fatally wounded Rachel. Gloria went into shock, and was framed for the murder. Vaughn was heavily represented by Singularity Investigations, but with help from Madrox and Monet, Vaughn confessed.

glot.name: Glot
glot.origin: Glot was a troll who existed on Earth during the Hyborian era. He spent his life terrorizing the primitive humans who lived in this time. When the future despot known as Hyperstorm banished Mister Fantastic to this era, he tried to live in relative seclusion where he tried to adapt modern technology in a vein hope of returning home to his proper era. During a test of a glider, he came across a young boy hiding in the cave in which he lived. Following the boy out to the danger he was clearly in, he crossed paths with Glot. Glot had the upper hand due to his superior strength and Reed's own doubts in himself; however, Reed eventually found the confidence to fight back and defeated Glot by launching him far away after turning his body into a sling shot. Glot's subsequent fate is unknown.

glow worm.name: Glow Worm
glow worm.origin: Rejected from even the Morlocks, Bulk and Glow Worm chose to live in a New Jersey hazardous waste dump. Wanting their lives to have meaning, they chose to attack X-Factor which at that time was posing as a group of mutant-hunters. They were defeated, the truth explained, and the situation diffused. Later, while they were dying from radiation poisoning, the High Evolutionary captured them. Mirage's temporary Valkyrie powers manifested death images for them. She was attached to a power draining device, so Bulk and Glow Worm sacrificed themselves to reverse the drain, which amplified her powers. Mirage and the New Mutants escaped the High Evolutionary's ship, leaving dead Bulk and Glow Worm behind. Glow Worm was presumably resurrected by the Five on the mutant nation of Krakoa. Glow Worm seemingly got engaged and was having a bachelor's party at a water park in New Jersey, but he was unfortunately turned into a monster by a spell casted by Margali Szardos.

glowboy.name: Glowboy
glowboy.origin: Glowboy was a young mutant forced out of his home when his powers activated at age fourteen. For a time he found refuge in a mutant community in the sewers, but had panic attacks when the wind was high. At one point he became indebted to the Kingpin, who had Glowboy's blood extracted in a drug lab run by him every four days as a source of DNA for the creation of Mutant Growth Hormone. Dr. Charlene McGowan, the scientist who extracted the blood samples, once commented that he always used to look tired.

gnarok.name: Gnarok
gnarok.origin: Gnarok was the god of doom, the death-god, among the Yggdars in a vale during the Hyborian Age. The Domain of Gnarok was told to be fiery, and was also called the "pits of the death-god". After an era of constant war between the Yggdars and the Ossiren, who had the ability to harness their psychic energy and use it to emit deadly eye blasts, the two groups came to live together harmoniously in the vale (although apart a group from another) for centuries. Eventually, during the Age of Conan, a cult of doom and hatred arose among one of the Yggdaar clan, dedicated to revere Gnarok and revive the ancient warriors ways, the ways of Gnarok. They worshiped an idol, the god-stone, to which they offered their loot as offerings. The blood-hungry doom cultists of the Yggdar clans, followers of Gnarok, eventually started attacking the Ossiren castles and killing their people, while the Yggdar elders, willing to live in peace the Ossiren, were unable to stop them. Attacking the cave of the cultists -along with the son of the Ossiren king- to root the group and allow the Ossiren and the peaceful Yggdars to live together harmoniously back again, Conan fell the god-stone upon the Yggdars, crushing them and breaking itself. The Ossiren prince then used his people's ability to blast the cave ceiling, crushing or entrapping the renegade Yggdars there, with him.

However, for whatever reasons, he set up a castle on Earth's Moon protected by an army of his Moon-Robots. Either through some unrecorded conflict or disrepair, his fortress became a shamble. go vin ng.name: Go Vin Ng
go vin ng.origin: Lt. Go Vin Ng was a member of the South Vietnamese army who was conducting a mission with an American army unit called the Half Fulls during the Vietnam War. During the mission in the jungle of Cambodia the members of the Half-Fulls stumbled upon the temple of the Dragon's Breadth Cult. There they meet Tai and the six brides of the cult. Tai made a pact with the men. Marry the six brides and the children from those unions would one day rule the world. Go Vin accepted the pack and he and his wife presumably went back to his home country of South Vietnam. Presumably they were killed as their daughter Min Li Ng was an orphan who knew nothing of her family history.

goat faced girl.name: Goat-Faced Girl
goat faced girl.origin: The Goat-Faced Girl is a member of Red Skull's S-Men with white fur and a goat's head. She, along with the rest of the S-Men, removed Professor X's body from his mausoleum in order to allow the Red Skull to take part of his brain and give himself telepathic powers, taking Rogue and Scarlet Witch as prisoners in the process. Along with the other S-Men, she accompanied the Red Skull to New York City. After Wolverine cut off the Red Skull's hand, she used her powers to disable his healing factor, allowing the mind-controlled Thor to knock him unconscious with Mjolnir. She escaped along with the other S-Men and the Red Skull after the tide of the battle turned in favor of the heroes. The Goat-Faced Girl was killed by Magneto, who had tracked down the Skull's activities after the villain turned Genosha into a mutant concentration camp.

goblin force.name: Goblin Force
goblin force.species: Unknown. Believed to be the shadow of the Phoenix
goblin force.origin: The Goblin Force was born at the beginning of reality during the Big Bang. Like the Phoenix Force it had limitless power, but unlike the Phoenix, it derived power from its ravenous hunger that could not be sated. Its hunger lead it to consume whole galaxies, when it encountered the Phoenix Force, the Phoenix stood against it only to be consumed. Even Galactus, the Devourer of Worlds, fell to the power of the Goblin Force's hunger. It was not until the 5th Host of the Celestials stood against the Goblin Force that it met defeat, though it was not destroyed. The Celestials were devestated from the battle, leaving the Goblin Force only to be contained. Many years later, the Goblin Force seized the opportunity to attach itself to the life force of Madelyne Pryor, making her its conduit into the world again, being reborn as the Goblin Queen through the corruption of Madelyne Pryor. As the Goblin Force gradually took over Madelyne's mind, it waged a war against Earth heroes, brainwashing most of them to join forces with her. Eventually, the Goblin Force was again contained by Scotty Summers, the son of Madelyne Pryor and Alex Summers who was said to have celestial level potential in power (similar to Franklin Richards); Madelyne Pryor was lost in the process. The Goblin Force eventually returned after possessing the comatose body of the Beyonder, adding his power to her own, and waged another war against Earth heroes joining forces with Dracula. Posing as the Beyonder, the Goblin Force killed most of Earth's heroes, including the X-Men, Fantastic Four, the Avengers, Doctor Doom, and Namor. The Goblin Force eventually revealed herself to Havok after stripping the Beyonder's body of its power. Havok was revealed to hold within him the Nexus of All Realities, an unlimited supply of energy funneled through him; using the Nexus, combined with Scotty's powers, the Goblin Force was separated from Madelyne and defeated.

goblyn.name: Goblyn
goblyn.origin: ===Origin=== Goblyn has an enormous skull, claws and hooves, and generally appears as her namesake. She was almost terminated as a fetus because her parents did not want to have a mutant child. It was obvious she was going to be a mutant because of her physical form. Even as a fetus her twin sister, Laura, was somehow able to save her by using her own power to open portals to send Goblyn to another dimension ("Liveworld"). At first, the two never met, and Laura unknowingly manifested her power to change places with Goblyn whenever she was extremely afraid. ===Derangers=== Laura was diagnosed autistic and withdrawn from the world. In an attempt to treat her autism, her parents sent her to the New Life Clinic, which was actually run by the insane villain Scramble. Laura managed to escape but was later caught by Bedlam and forced to become a member of his team of Derangers. Bedlam used Laura and Goblyn against Alpha Flight. She was the only one of his team of mind controlled super-humans to survive the final battle with him. She was soon inducted into Beta Flight, under the mistaken belief that Laura was Goblyn and that she could change form. ===Sisters Meet=== Finally, the two met each other when the Dreamqueen threatened Laura, making her subconsciously summon Alpha Flight. After she and Goblyn escaped, Laura came out of her shell, and the sisters grew extremely close. When they returned to Earth, and Alpha Flight disbanded, Laura and Goblyn went to live with Purple Girl. ===Beta Flight=== They re-joined Beta Flight when Talisman dispatched them on a quest for Northstar, thanks to Laura`s ability to open portals to other dimensions. The two stayed on when the team was once again funded by the government and Department H was re-formed. However, both were severely injured when Wild Child went insane and attacked them. Laura sent Goblyn instinctively to Liveworld and had to return with Beta Flight to save her. Once they returned from Liveworld, Goblyn and Beta Flight were temporarily demoted to Gamma Flight for their poor showing. After an effective field operation during the Infinity War, however, they once again became active as Beta Flight, the official second team of heroes working for Department H. Since the disbanding of Alpha Flight after the clash with the Hardliners, resulting in the subsequent disbanding of Beta Flight, both Dean sisters left Department H. Goblyn's current status is unknown.

god of the watch.name: God of the Watch
god of the watch.origin: After Gorr the God Butcher attacked the Halls of All-Knowing, the God of the Watch arrived to complete a standard investigation of the incident. The candid god gave his report to the Lord Librarian, informing the annoyed fairy that Omnipotence City had been attempting to hail Chronux to no avail. Unaware to the severe threat the God Butcher held and believing his task to be done, he requested to be excused, but not before the Lord Librarian ordered him to summon the Parliament of Pantheons, stunning him.

god killer.name: God-Killer
god killer.origin: A survivor from the Uncreated mass suicide, who was captured by the Shi'ar. When it first awoke after it's capture, it entered a state of madness killing everything and wanting to know if the Shi'ar worshipped a god, just so it could find and kill it. More recently Vulcan released God-Killer from prison and recruited it into his Imperial Guard. The Praetorians were captured on Kree-Lar by Nova Prime, and imprisoned on Nu-Xandar (Ego) for their war crimes against their Nova Corps prisoners. When Ego took back control of himself, he was transferred to Zan Philo's Corps starship Resolute Duty.

goddess.name: Goddess
goddess.species: The good portion of Adam Warlock's soul given life.
goddess.origin: The Goddess, along with her counterpart The Magus, was created while Adam Warlock was briefly in possession of the Infinity Gauntlet; desiring to be a logical god, and not prone to judgment-impairing emotions, Warlock subconsciously expelled both good and evil from his soul, creating the beings The Goddess and The Magus respectively. Neither stayed inactive, and both resurfaced. The first hint of The Goddess' existence came at the end of the Infinity War crossover, when it was revealed that an unknown woman had stolen the five Cosmic Containment Units in the Magus' possession. Thanos suspected the Goddess' existence and threat to the universe. When The Goddess made her appearance, reaching out to the heroes of Earth who were of a religious or spiritual persuasion as their would-be savior, she possessed 30 Cosmic Cubes, gathered from a multitude of different realities, which she soon reformed into the enormous structure known as the Cosmic Egg. The Egg afforded the wielder a phenomenal amount of power, although it still fell short of the legendary Infinity Gauntlet, most notably in its lack of control over the soul. She recruited various heroes to join her in her mission to create peace throughout the universe, and created her base on Paradise Omega. From her base on the newly-reformed Counter-Earth, The Goddess used her Earth heroes and Cosmic Egg to declare holy war on a sinful universe, claiming that she was the chosen servant of the Living Tribunal's Master, or the "Supreme One" (aka the One-Above-All). Despite being the "good" portion of Adam Warlock's soul, she was a creature of extremes, and saw only extreme solutions to the problems she perceived; in this case, she decided at some point that the only way to remove all sin was to remove all sinners by blowing the Universe up. Using heavy telepathic emissions from the Egg, The Goddess slowly removed all crime, hate and war from everywhere across the galaxy, with seemingly the only ones unaffected being Earth's "heretical" heroes, and Uatu the Watcher. She stopped Mister Fantastic, Iron Man, and the Vision from investigating her base on Paradise Omega. As the heroes plotted against the Goddess, Pip the Troll teleported into Paradise Omega and used the Cosmic Egg to temporarily change the Goddess into salt, although this effort to stop her ended in failure. Ultimately, it was Thanos of Titan, in conjunction with Warlock and the heretic heroes, who engineered the defeat of The Goddess. Believing she had triggered the celestial armageddon she had worked for, The Goddess was dismayed to learn that Warlock's spirit had communicated with the Egg, sending out an illusion that armageddon had been triggered, a fraction of a second before the real thing. This meant that The Goddess' plans were ruined; since her many universal followers now realized her intent, she could not generate the universal will needed to override the Egg's inbuilt safeguards regarding destruction. The climax came in a showdown on the spiritual plane between The Goddess, the soul of Adam Warlock (now linked with the Cosmic Egg through his own machinations), Thanos (powered by Adam's Soul Gem, which he had been given for the duration of the conflict), and Professor X (catatonic, but with Thanos able to access his spirit on the astral plane). The Goddess evaded their attacks, but when she returned to the physical plane to utilise the Egg's energies against the heroes, she found that Adam Warlock had beaten her to it, taking control of the Egg long enough to stall her, during which period Thanos used the power of the Soul Gem to take her spirit within, to Soulworld. Within Soul World, The Goddess met with her counterpart, The Magus; the two made to battle, but it transpired that, as part-souls themselves, not only could they not interact with the other denizens of Soulworld, but they could not even touch each other. As The Magus put it: "Even to each other we are as ghosts." Over time, The Magus apparently escaped the Soul World. It is unclear at this point if the Goddess has escaped as well, but she has not since made a reappearance.
