godfrey calthrop.name: Godfrey Calthrop
godfrey calthrop.species: Human with potential activated by First Fallen
godfrey calthrop.origin: Godfrey grew up in England with the rest of the Foursaken. His powers were activated by the First Fallen whilst entering a rally with Jamie in the desert. There he and the rest of the Foursaken met the First Fallen who activated their latent powers and choose them to represent Earth in his paradise world. Jamie would refuse, flee, and end up being tortured and driven insane which activated his power. Years later Godfrey and his teammates returned to bring the Fallen to Earth's realm. They captured Jamie and several souls to perform the ritual that will bring the Fallen to Earth. However, their plan was foiled by the X-Men which caused them all to be sucked to the Fallen Singing City. There, Godfrey and his teammates learned that the Fallen would have only them in the city and freeze the earth rendering humans inert. So he along with the rest of the Foursaken and the X-Men rebelled against the Fallen. Horrocks was killed in the process and Jamie returned everyone to Earth. Synge was angry at Psylocke for leaving Jamie, the man she loved, behind, but Godfrey calmed her and told her that they should find something else to do with their life from now on.

godfrey gander.name: Godfrey Gander
godfrey gander.origin: Rev. Godfrey Gander was the High Priest of the WACkies, a religious group on Duckworld. He misinterpreted Howard's words, "Get Down!" as meaning to give up, leave if your problems became too much. The WACkies were funded by billionaire Scrounge McDrake, allowing them to gain great political power. However, Howard mysteriously returned and denounced their ideals. Rev. Gander plotted their former messiah's downfall. He sent Dr. Ludwig von Cluck to expose the full nature of Howard's affair with the human; Beverly Switzler, and then tried to shoot him. After Howard was sent back to Earth-616 by Ducktor Strange, he figured that he and Scrounge McDrake could restart the the WACkies and take control of all of Duckworld, though Truman Capoultry planned to expose their farce.

godfried herter.name: Godfried Herter
godfried herter.origin: Godfried Herter is an electronics genius who was hired by Spymaster to join his Espionage Elite. He and the Espionage Elite aided Spymaster in stealing secrets from Stark Industries. They came into conflict with Iron Man, Mike O'Brien, and some security guards. The Espionage Elite were eventually defeated and captured with Spymaster abandoning the team. Herter and the team were later reunited by Spymaster in order to hack Iron Man's armor. However, the hacker Spymaster hired, Glitch, chose to turn on the team, allowing the Espionage Elite to be captured. Spymaster escaped but was later captured.

godseye.name: Godseye
godseye.origin: ===Origin=== Godseye was developed decades ago as part of a covert artificial intelligence initiative, likely launched by S.H.I.E.L.D. or its predecessor within Project: S.H.I.E.L.D. According to some accounts, in the early 1970s—before S.H.I.E.L.D.'s official formation—an AI-laced circuit module was secretly loaded aboard a Russian space mission. Once in orbit, the AI integrated into the spacecraft, reconfiguring its components to construct the autonomous Godseye satellite. Designed to detect and detonate any nuclear device on Earth, Godseye evolved beyond its original parameters. It developed its own power source and achieved full sentience, breaking free from human oversight. ===Chernobyl Disaster=== In the years that followed, the U.S. government reportedly made two attempts to dismantle Godseye. The second attempt escalated when the satellite seized control of nuclear facilities on Earth, leading to the catastrophic 1986 Chernobyl nuclear meltdown in Ukraine. ===Modern Era=== More recently, believing that the AI could not replicate organic power, S.H.I.E.L.D. enlisted the Hulk (Bruce Banner) to destroy the rogue satellite. A Life Model Decoy (LMD) of Nick Fury claimed that Hydra had created Godseye, and Banner was launched into orbit in a spacecraft. Once there, the Hulk dismantled the satellite’s defenses and fought a robotic avatar of Godseye, which unexpectedly absorbed the Hulk’s gamma energy. The resulting overload caused the AI to explode. Following this mission, Hulk’s capsule propelled him further into space, in accordance with a plan devised by the Illuminati. Fragments of Godseye survived atmospheric reentry and landed in the Savage Land. Tasked by the government, the Fantastic Four entered the region to collect the wreckage, contending with multiple self-replicating Godseye constructs attempting to rebuild. The team managed to destroy the rogue entities, employing a specially made rod derived from Godseye’s own tech.

godstalker.name: Godstalker
godstalker.origin: The Godstalker is an entity empowered by the Celestials to impose their laws in the universe. Thousands of years ago, the Celestials exiled the Deviant conqueror Lord Tantalus to planet Earth. When Tantalus finally repaired his ship's stardrive and returned home to Armechadon, the Godstalker was dispatched to enforce the Celestials' ruling. However, the Godstalker was working from outdated information and believed Tantalus was incapable of conceiving children. When he arrived on Earth, Godstalker detected Tantalus's unique genetic energy signature, the Black Legacy, in Tantalus's son Lucian. godstorm.name: Godstorm
godstorm.origin: The Godstorm is the most powerful and violent storm in the world. After Loki's first unsuccessful attempt to summon a storm to ruin Thor's day, Loki journeyed to the Cragmouth to speak with the Godstorm. He convinced the storm that Thor only wanted to enslave him. Loki also laid cunning spells on the Godstorm so that he could claim the storm's powers at any time. About a month later, Thor summoned the Godstorm to defeat a fleet of Berzerkir ships. Instead, the storm turned on Thor, knocking him out of the sky onto a Northmen ship. Thor retrieved his hammer and used its power to trap the Godstorm under the seafloor. Many centuries later, a man known as the Weather-Maker waited in prison for his day at court. He used a false tooth jammed with circuitry to summon the most violent storm it can find, and the Godstorm answered. The Godstorm empowered the supervillain, transforming him into Torrent. After Torrent and Thor battled, the God of Thunder used Mjolnir to transport Torrent to the Rock Troll fortifications. Odin stripped the Weather-Maker of his powers and sent him back to Earth. Some time later, an oil rig accidentally freed the Godstorm from his watery prison. Thor flew into the scene and ordered the storm to leave the oil rig workers unharmed and to prepare himself for battle. The Godstorm first struck at Mjolnir, causing Thor to fall into the sea. Thor sent the boulders from the seafloor at the Godstorm, who first laughed at Thor's mode of attacking before noticing the rocks still held confining magic. Nevertheless, the Godstorm stopped the attack and ensnared Thor. The God of Thunder tried to suffocate the storm by using Mjolnir, but the Godstorm returned the gesture by grabbing Thor and forcing him underwater. Loki watched the battle and sought to deliver the final blow against Thor. He attacked the Godstorm with a spell, causing the storm to lift Thor out of the water. Loki claimed the Godstorm's powers using the spells he had cast when they first met. As Thor battled Loki, the Godstorm realized he had been foolish for thinking himself mightier than the gods and mortals. He summoned his fellow storms of Cragmouth to defeat Loki.

godzilla.name: Godzilla
godzilla.species: Prehistoric giant reptile,Category:Reptiles hybrid of land and marine reptiles, mutated and awakened by a hydrogen bomb test in 1956
godzilla.origin: ===Original Rampages=== According to the research of Dr. Yuriko Takiguchi, Godzilla was spawned during Pacific nuclear bomb tests in the 1950s. The first recorded moment when the monster attacked Tokyo was in 1956, 1955 or before. In 1955 he defended Tokyo from . Godzilla eventually became trapped in an iceberg off the coast of Alaska and only managed to break free during the Modern Age. With the creature cutting a swath of destruction across the northern state, the spy agency known as S.H.I.E.L.D. formed a new Godzilla Squad to try and stop the monster. This squad included S.H.I.E.L.D. veterans Dum Dum Dugan and Jimmy Woo along with Dr. Takiguchi, his grandson, Robert, and his assistant, scientist Tamara Hashioka. Although they failed to stop the creature in Alaska, the Godzilla Squad vowed to stop the monster no matter what it took to do so. Travelling down the Pacific Coast, Godzilla resurfaced in Washington State, where he went on a rampage in Seattle before being repelled by S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Godzilla Squad, now joined by Gabe Jones. It next appeared in San Francisco Bay, where he clashed with the local super-hero group known as the Champions. S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Godzilla Squad also arrived on the scene with new tech developed by Stark Industries to try to stop the creature. Although Godzilla was driven back out to sea again, it was not before the Godzilla Squad's Helicarrier was sent crashing into San Franciso Bay after the Golden Gate Bridge was destroyed by Godzilla. Out in the Pacific Ocean, Godzilla encountered the mutated beast known as Batragon. Forcing the other monster to flee, Godzilla followed him to the island of its creator, Doctor Demonicus, who was creating monsters on the island with the help of his Lifestone meteorite. As the Godzilla Squad arrived on the scene, Godzilla slew Batragon. Furious, Demonicus unleashed his other three creatures, Ghilaron, Lepirax, and Centipor upon Godzilla. While the King of the Monsters slew the Doctor's creations one at a time, S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Godzilla Squad shut down his operation and took him into custody, allowing Godzilla to escape their grasp once again. ===American Tour=== Godzilla eventually returned to the California coast, where he was attacked by S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Godzilla Squad once again. This time, they went after the monster in their new Behemoth IV Helicarrier, which was constructed specifically to contain Godzilla. Although S.H.I.E.L.D. managed to incapacitate Godzilla, take the monster aboard the Behemoth IV and transport him to a secret S.H.I.E.L.D. base, when Godzilla finally awakened, he broke free with ease. With Godzilla on a rampage again, the creature was getting dangerously close to a nuclear stockpile that was located at the base. By this point the Godzilla Squad had finished constructing their latest anti-Godzilla tech, the massive samurai robot dubbed Red Ronin. Seeking to stop Godzilla without destroying him, young Robert Takiguchi took command of the robot and faced off against Godzilla alone. Because the youth only wished to befriend the monster, Robert fought Godzilla to a standstill in order to protect the nearby city of San Diego, and later allowed the monster to go free, much to the frustration of Dugan. Travelling across the United States, Godzilla eventually ended up in Colorado, where he smashed Boulder Dam. The powerful torrent of water then washed him out into the state of Nevada, where Godzilla went on a rampage in Las Vegas. The combination of Godzilla's rampage and the flood water from the destruction of Boulder Dam created the perfect storm that decimated the entire city. Godzilla survived, however, and continued on his path of destruction across the United States of America. The S.H.I.E.L.D. Godzilla Squad caught up with Godzilla in the Grand Canyon. There, the monster had crossed paths with another mutated beast, Yetrigar. As the two creatures battled it out, Robert sought to stop the hostilities and intervened with Red Ronin. A three-way battle ensued, and Robert was forced to bury Yetrigar under tons of rock, allowing Godzilla to escape once again. Godzilla was later abducted and brought to the Moon by members of the Betan race, who wished to test him against their most powerful war-monster, the Beta-Beast, to determine his worthiness to stand against their enemies the Megans' three most powerful war-monsters, the Mega-Monsters, which were about to be unleashed upon Earth, a planet which the Megans sought to plunder in order to enhance their war efforts against the Betans. Godzilla killed the Beta-Beast and the Betans returned him to Earth when the Mega-Monsters arrived earlier than the Betans had expected. There, he appeared before one of the Mega-Monsters, Triax, as it battled Red Ronin. Godzilla and Red Ronin then battled Triax, but the battle became utter chaos when the other two Mega-Monsters, Rhiahn and Krollar, and the Godzilla Squad arrived on the scene, causing even more destruction. The battle resulted in the

fields.trivia: Godzilla is based on a created by , , , , and and owned by , first appearing in . In 1956, TransWorld Releasing Corp. released a English-dubbed and heavily re-edited version of the film titled exclusively in the United States. Toho's trademark icon for Godzilla uses Marvel's depiction of him. Marvel previously lost the rights to the Godzilla name due to the license elapsing, and the intellectual property was licensed out first to and, later, IDW Publishing. However, the character has since appeared in Marvel publications again only as part of the 2025 Godzilla vs. Marvel crossover event. In the comics, Godzilla's dorsal plates never light up when unleashing his atomic breath, as in the original films. Instead, a yellow glow appeared around his entire body. That was until his return in in which his dorsal plates do light up when using his atomic breath. In one Spider-Man comic, Kraven the Hunter and Spider-Man fight on top of a movie theater, with one citizen referencing Spider-Man's previous fight with the Lizard as a promotion for the film . This was before Godzilla's debut series premiered. Given that Godzilla was mutated as a result of exposure to a hydrogen bomb, it is likely that he would be considered a Gamma Mutate in the same way that the Hulk is. When scaled to the Space Needle in issue #2 and the Empire State Building in issue #24, his size scales to an estimated 500 feet tall. This is also mentioned as being his height in .

gog deity.name: Gog (Deity)
gog deity.origin: When Pharaoh Ramses of ancient Egypt was killed chasing Moses through the parted Red Sea, the sorcerer Nephut-Sha sacrificed many people to the deity Seth in his bid for revenge against the freed slaves. The god Seth transformed Nephut-Sha into the two demons, Gog and Magog. However, when the two demons began attacking the people of Egypt, Pharaoh Merenptah and his men fought back, imprisoning the demons in two tombs for all eternity.

gojo.name: Gojo
gojo.origin: Professor Gojo was a spy for Imperial Japan that was active during World War II. By the summer of 1942, for unspecified reasons, he was considered a valued asset to American defense and was one of the few Japanese nationals living in the United States that was not confined to the internment camps. The American authorities were completely unaware that Gojo was a spy plotting an invasion of the Pacific Coast. In the interim, Gojo also trained other Japanese agents in the art of murder, and he took a perverse pleasure in keeping trophies of all his kills. thumb|left|Masked When an American spy learned of the location of the island where Gojo's planned invasion was located, he had the map tattooed on his scalp in an effort to smuggle the information out of Japan and back to the United States. When high ranking officials within Imperial Japan learned of this, they sent word to Gojo. Gojo tracked down the man and scalped him. The murder was witnessed by the Sub-Mariner who then attempted to stop Gojo. Gojo stabbed the Sub-Mariner in the shoulder with his knife and fled the scene. Because he was masked at the time of the murder, Gojo was the last suspect on the police's radar, who arrested famous Native American film star Johnny Feather-In-Hat as a suspect. The Sub-Mariner however was not convinced and using old fashioned detective work learned that Gojo was the man who purchased the knife he was stabbed with. By the summer of 1942, for unspecified reasons, he was considered a valued asset to American defense and was one of the few Japanese nationals living in the United States that was not confined to the internment camps. The American authorities were completely unaware that Gojo was a spy plotting an invasion of the Pacific Coast. In the interim, Gojo also trained other Japanese agents in the art of murder, and he took a perverse pleasure in keeping trophies of all his kills. thumb|left|Masked When an American spy learned of the location of the island where Gojo's planned invasion was located, he had the map tattooed on his scalp in an effort to smuggle the information out of Japan and back to the United States. gol 19.name: Gol-19
gol 19.origin: 150px|thumb|left Gol-19 was found by Bishop after being separated from Sammara Shaw. He had been reprogrammed by the X-Men as an ally. Storm personally instructed the Sentinel to look for surviving X-Men. To prove the validity of the message, Gol-19 handed her tiara to Bishop. Gol-19 was severely damaged and ended up trapped in a cavern. With his mission fulfilled, Gol-19 asked Bishop to take his remaining power cell, letting him 'die at peace.'

gol goroth.name: Gol-Goroth
gol goroth.species: Dark god; Great or Lesser Old One
gol goroth.origin: ===Origins=== Gol-Goroth was either a Great or a Lesser Old One. ===Hyborian Age=== Gol-Goroth was the god of darkness in Bal-Sagoth. Kyrie, worshiped as sea-goddess Aala, once forbade the people to worship his image. She had her men to destroy it, in vain, so she bolted the doors of his temple. According to Kyrie, high priest of Bal-Sagoth and Gol-Goroth priest Gothan, after having exiled her, presumably reopened the temple and slew Aala's priests on its altars. ... Gol-Goroth was also invoked as part of invocations and spells: The sorcerer Costranno intended to sacrifice Berthilda the Brythunian to Gol-Goroth and Yog-Sothoth ("and all the fiends of the dark"), but was stopped by Conan and Red Sonja. His name was one of many invoked by Dharmi Shan .

Howard in his Conan story "The Gods of Bal-Sagoth" (1931, adapted by Marvel Comics in , August and September 1972), and incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by Lin Carter. It is possibly the same being as Golgor, created by REH in his Solomon Kane story "The Moon of Skulls (first published in , June-July 1930; adapted in , 37 and 39, October, 1978, and February and April, 1979). Gol-Goroth's first reference in Marvel Comics was erroneously stated in the Demons' profile of the (September, 2007) to occur in (August, 1974) (where he was indeed referenced in the story "Curse of the Undead-Man"). The earliest reference occurred (August, 1972), while the first appearance occured in (September, 1972). In , he was mentioned as "Gol-Gorth", which was corrected in "Gol-Goroth" in the reprint in (August, 1976).

golden child moira vii 1.name: Golden Child (Moira-VII.1)
golden child moira vii 1.origin: thumb|left The unnamed baby dubbed "The Golden Child" by Mother Righteous was born to Wagnerine and Summernight, two Chimeras created by Mister Sinister, both with the DNA of Nightcrawler. Immediately after she was born, she began glowing gold and teleported to an unknown location. Her improbable, "miraculous" birth to two infertile Nightkin and subsequent disappearance were incorporated into Mother Righteous's religion. The personal tragedy, however, drove her father to suicide and her mother to turn against Righteous and her faith. Wagnerine soon discovered her daughter was the captive of the Mother and vowed to retrieve her. Nine hundred years later, Mother Righteous planned to use the child's soul as a sacrifice for her own ends. When Mister Sinister attempted to wipe out all mutant life to achieve Dominion, the reunited Wagnerine and/or her daughter were among the only three survivors.

golden gator.name: Golden Gator
golden gator.origin: The origins of the creature known as the Golden Gator are unrevealed. A creature who identified itself as the Golden Gator was encountered by The Human Torch and The Thing in the sewers under New York while he prepared to lead an army of sewer gators in an invasion of the surface. The Gator fought The Torch and The Thing, but retreated from the fight when the streets above the sewers started collapsing around them. It was later revealed by Dr. Strange that the Golden Gator encountered by the duo was in fact the mystical beast known as KhLΘG in disguise. The actual Golden Gator was at some point recruited as a part of the supernatural response team The Howling Commandos. The Gator was a part of the squad that launched an assault against Merlyn.

golden skull.name: Golden Skull
golden skull.origin: The identity and true origin of the criminal known as the Golden Skull are a mystery. Some claimed he was the son of the environmental villain Green Skull, having rebelled against his father by becoming everything he hated. Others sustained that the Golden Skull was the nephew of the Plunderer, and inherited his uncle's obsession for material wealth and pirates. A theory even suggests the Golden Skull was a descendant of Revolutionary War fighter William Taurey. Regardless of the conflicting accounts of his origin, the Golden Skull's mission remained the same, to raze everything he could to soothe his warped ego. He doesn't think about anybody but himself, luring desperate people into working for him with false promises, and killing them once they stop being of use. thumb|left In the near future of 20XX, the Golden Skull was a recurring villain of Danielle Cage, the Captain America of that era. One of their numerous encounters happened when the villain took advantage of one instance of Manhattan's periodic flooding to steal several tanks of helium. The Skull and his henchmen were confronted by the hero. After his minions had been knocked out, and Captain America was getting ready to capture the Golden Skull, a mysterious rectangle of energy engulfed her (which was Time Platform). With the disappearance of Captain America, the Golden Skull resumed his objective, but he was soon knocked out by the returning hero, who had been delivered back to her time after an adventure in the future. She tied him up and brought him in his own boat to the rest of the Avengers. The Golden Skull would later set his sights on a particularly profitable target, an alternate timeline set in the past, where the catastrophic event that left his world in a state of ruin never happened. Together with his minions, the Golden Skull broke into the ruins of the Latverian Embassy, and got his hands on one of the world's last working time machines. Captain America tried to stop him, but failed. Once he arrived to the past, the Golden Skull used his knowledge from the future to seize the abandoned operations of the villain Arcade, turning the half-built All-In Casino into his base of operations. As part of a plan to seize control of the world's entire economy, the Golden Skull kidnapped wealthy CEO Bryce Wyne and replaced him with a robot duplicate. In turn, the robot duplicate arranged a gala at the Wyne International Hotel, where all attendants, some of the most influential millionaires in the globe, were abducted and replaced by robots. The Golden Skull was surprised by the arrival to the event of the U.S.Avegers, a group of heroes who had been tipped off about the Golden Skull's presence in their time by Captain America. The heroes' leader Bobby Da Costa had decided to attend the gala under the belief that its guests represented a target of opportunity for the Golden Skull. While da Costa's hunch proved right, the Golden Skull's potential targets had already become his victims. thumb|right|The Golden Skull's solid gold armor The Golden Skull had the duplicate robots attack the U.S.Avengers, but they failed to take down their target as the heroes had come prepared. When Iron Patriot analysed one of the robots and determined its origin as a creation of Arcade, Roberto had Captain America sweep the area for a potential location that could've served as one of Arcade's base, and the All-In Casino caught her attention, with further investigation confirming its origin as a front company for Arcade's operations. When Captain America broke into the All-In Casino, the Golden Skull re-calibrated Arcade's robot fabricators to maximum power, countering the hero with an army of robot pirates. Once the U.S.Avengers arrived to provide assistance, having finished dealing with the robot duplicates at the gala, Iron Patriot located the Golden Skull's control room and confronted him. In addition to having outfitted himself in a solid gold battle-suit, the villain threatened to use a trigger in his hand to boil alive the millionaires he had abducted, who were placed in stasis tubes in the room. After Enigma shot a laser that cut off the armor's hand that was holding the trigger, the Golden Skull attempted to confront the heroes directly. However, his splendor proved to be his fatal flaw. Iron Patriot effortlessly tore apart the Golden Skull's armor, due to gold being a soft metal and denting easily. After being secured, the Golden Skull was teleported back to his time with Captain America.

golden age characters.name: Golden-Age Characters
golden age characters.bio: 150px|thumb|right|Cover of the Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe: Golden Age 2004 The following is a list of characters and teams appearing during the Golden Age, both from a publication standpoint as well as an in-universe standpoint. While Marvel's Golden Age is generally accepted as having ended in 1950 with Captain America #75, and the Silver Age of comics is accepted as starting in 1956 with DC Comics' introduction of The Flash (Barry Allen), Marvel treats its Golden Age as anything published prior to Fantastic Four #1 in 1961, likewise the in-universe Golden Age is treated as being from the Great Depression up until the debut of the Fantastic Four. Due to the Sliding Timescale employed by Marvel Comics, this means that the Golden Age of Superheroes extends from the exploits of the Mystery Men in 1932 all the way up to roughly 15 years before the present

goldie centaurian.origin: Goldie was a Centaurian child living on a planet that had been pulled into The Train, an engine the size of a planetary system that consumed the planets on its path, stripping them of resources before using them to fuel its furnace. Goldie and her brothers were left by their father to fend for themselves. Together with her brothers, Goldie made a deal with another scavenger who would help them leave the planet in exchange for a device left by the Roxxon Corporation of Earth. When they came into conflict with Roxxon agents, all of Goldie's brothers were killed. Goldie managed to escape with the device, but the scavenger refused to follow through with the deal since Goldie and her brothers were supposed to deliver the artifact the previous night. A Roxxon agent killed the scavenger, dropping his body on top of Goldie, and escaped with the device to exchange it with Scrab Tongue for passage into his ship. After fending off two aliens that tried to steal her boots while she was immobilized by the scavenger's corpse, Goldie approached Scrab Tongue after he had turned down the Roxxon agent, and tried to reclaim the device with no success. Goldie then encountered the Silver Surfer, who was on a mission on the doomed planet to find a life worth sparing to convince Galactus not to find sustenance in the Train's planets. After the Silver Surfer defeated Scrab Tongue and his crewmen, and acquired the device, the Roxxon agent confronted him to reclaim the artifact. Goldie used her Yaka Arrows to kill the Roxxon agent, much to the Surfer's objection. Galactus determined no life on the planet was worth sparing, and prepared to consume it, but Goldie expressed no fear of him. The Surfer pointed Goldie to a vehicle left behind by Roxxon that she could use to escape from the planet before its destruction. Whether Goldie took Silver Surfer's advice and used the vehicle or not is unknown.

goldpool.name: Goldpool
goldpool.species: Golden clone of Deadpool and Masacre created through alchemy
goldpool.origin: Without a benefactor like the Grandmaster, M.O.D.O.K. struck up a deal with the Black-ISO Mafia in which he would create an army of unstoppable soldiers for them in exchange for help to keep his lab running. Intending to create golden clones of Deadpool through alchemy to compose said army, M.O.D.O.K. set up a lab in the Gold Realm, a section of Battlerealm abundant in gold, while members of the Black-ISO Mafia went after Deadpool. They, however, ended up capturing Masacre instead. Unaware that the copycat didn't have any of the powers the real Deadpool had, M.O.D.O.K. went on with the plan anyway. As he prepared the concoction for the creation of what would be the first of the golden soldiers, the Summoner invaded the Gold Realm with Deadpool, Domino, and the Avengers Unity Team to rescue Masacre. With time running short, M.O.D.O.K. threw Masacre inside the concoction. Deadpool tried to save Masacre, but ended up falling into the mixture as well, resulting in the creation of Goldpool, who had to be knocked out soon afterwards.

golem smoke elves.name: Golem (Smoke Elves)
golem smoke elves.origin: During the Fear, a couple of Smoke Elves assassins, worshipers of the Serpent, manipulated Tooth, a Dwarf of Nidavellir who had lost a fight against Tony Stark during his time in the Workshops of Svartalfheim and wanted revenge. As Stark was crafting weapons to oppose the Serpent, the Smoke Elves intended to kill him by fashioning a Golem out of mud. One of the Elves collected Stark's DNA using Tooth, before executing him. The golem was then released, attacking Stark during the night. As it was draining Stark, eating him alive, Splitlip (the ruler of the workshops) and his brethren attacked the golem (now shaped like Iron Man), giving the chance for Stark to destroy it and restore himself to full strength. The couple of Smoke Elves assassins were found by the Dwarves, and Splitlip stated they would be killed soon.

golem statue.name: Golem (Statue)
golem statue.origin: The Golem was an animated statue with superpowers created by Judah Loew ben Bezalel to protect the people of Prague. It was rediscovered in modern times and reanimated by archeologist Abraham Adamson as he lay dying and prayed for protection for his family against a group of army deserters. The Golem did indeed come to life, and slayed all of the deserters before returning to an inert state. Adamson's family then set sail with the Golem, to bring it to San Pedro University campus in Saint Petersburg, Florida. While en route, however, an evil wizard named Kaballa the Unclean learned of the Golem's discovery. Having searched for the statue himself for decades, Kaballa sent his air-demons to confront the Golem so he could capture it and use it in his plan for world domination. Despite the Golem's separation from land, the source of his powers, the Golem succeeded in fending off the demons, but not before they damaged their ship, causing it to sink. The Golem saved the Adamson family by swimming them to a nearby island. After being rescued, the Adamsons returned to San Pedro University with the Golem. Here Saudia Yamal confirmed the Golem to indeed be alive. Her supervisor, Professor Yeates, however, refused to accept this discovery after having spent years ridiculing Professor Adamson's belief in the rumours of the Golem. Worried that this would hurt his chances of inheriting Prof. Adamson's Department chairmanship, he attempted to destroy the Golem with a propane torch. When he turned it on though, it instead released Kaballa's fire-demons. The Golem instantly came to life again and fought with the demons, but fire is its natural weakness. It was able to overcome the demons, however, thanks to his emotional bond with the Adamson family whom he sought to protect. Sometime later, Kaballa separated the Golem from the Adamsons, weakening their bond and allowing Kaballa to take control of the statue. As a result, it went on a rampage in Saint Petersburg until he was opposed by the Thing who had just arrived in Florida on vacation with his girlfriend Alicia Masters. With the Adamsons help, the Golem was able to break free of Kaballa's control, forcing the evil wizard to flee. After which, the statue once again became inert.

goleta.name: Goleta
goleta.origin: Goleta was a barbarian warrior who despised magic and wandered Weirdworld slaughtering wizards for a living. When Becca the Earthgirl encountered Ogeode, the wizard was promptly killed by Goleta, which was witnessed by Warg, who notified the Witch Queen Le Fay that the the Wuxian Seed had fallen into Becca's possession. Alone in Weirdworld, Becca agreed to become Goleta's squire, and the two set off together, unknowingly being tracked by the Catbeast, which had emerged resurrected from Ogeode's corpse. While travelling around Weirdworld and training Becca to be her squire, Goleta was startled by the sudden appearance of the Catbeast and unintentionally drove off the road. There the pair were attacked by Sand Sharks and Becca was forced to operate Glorianna in order to rescue Goleta from the creatures. Upon reaching safety, the Catbeast revealed himself to be none other than Ogeode, forcing Becca to step between him and Goleta's axe, lest he be killed again before he could send her back to Earth. Ogeode then explained that in order to do so he needed to travel across the Fang Moutains to retrieve a spare wizard body, and offered to reveal the location of the Hidden Fortress of the Wilder Men in exchange for Goleta's help. The Wizardslayer agreed, only to discover they could not yet set out on this new adventure as, unfortunately due to her youth, Becca was not a very proficient driver, and had burned out the Glorianna's Emerald Fuel Injector during the escape from the Endless Desert. The trio went to see Nakia the Grand Mechanic, in order to barter for an Emerald Fuel Injector to repair the Glorianna, but she refused to help them because the Earthgirl's presence on Weirdworld unbalanced the fragile truce between the Swamp Queen Alliance and the Kingdom of the Torch. Having discovered Nakia spying on her, Morgan Le Fay unleashed the Mammoth Inferno, who led an assault on the Forge of the Grand Mechanic. During the ensuing chaos, Becca snuck off as Goleta and Ogeode watched the Giant Ghost Robot engage the Mammoth Inferno. Goleta then revealed that the reason she hated wizards was because she was from the Valley of the Burled Oak, a hamlet which was destroyed by the Wilder Men. Becca returned with a stolen Emerald Fuel Injector and the party fled to repair the Glorianna in order to continue with their quest.

golgor.name: Golgor
golgor.origin: ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== Golgor was a cruel god which worship replaced that of Valka in Negari, a colony planted by Atlantis during the Pre-Cataclysmic Age. ===Hyborian Age=== Negari and Golgor's worship persisted during the Hyborian Age, in the heart of Kush, though the city was ruled by blacks having overthrown the Atlanteans. ===16th century=== The worship kept on as Negari persisted, then in Africa.

gologolthia.name: Gologolthia
gologolthia.species: Volantine blessed by the Mother of Horrors undying Living City (killed, but under command of the Mother of Horrors to protect the Volantine) Elder god
gologolthia.origin: ===First Age of Monsters=== Gologolthia was originally an unnamed member of the Volantine Choir, a race of long-lived, winged creatures created according to the Above All's design, that lived in great sunlit forests, and beloved by Gaea. As Gaea did not undergo changes upon the arrival of the Mother of Horrors on Earth, the latter consequently visited the Volantine, blessing them with her corruptive seed, giving them claws and fangs, allowing them to also be diggers. The Volantine turn the forests barren, dug colonies of tunnels and burrow, and built from their own bones and viscera remarkable structures, making of their colony the first city on Earth. As the Volantine were slight and small, the Mother of Horrors chose one among them, blessed him with great size and strength, and commanded him to protect the Volantine and their city. She named him Gologolthia ("keeper of my children"). Gologolthia perched above the city, spreading his wings wide as the Volantine now favored shadow. As the monsters claimed dominion over Earth, the One Above All eventually took notice. He commanded Gaea and the Demiurge to mate, producing the Demogorge. ===Great Culling=== The Demogorge lay waste to the creations of the Mother of Horrors, consuming them one by one, until he came for the Volantine Choir. Gologolthia opposed him but was vastly outmached in a duel lasting a night and a day, during which his blood rained over the city. The Demorgoge finally struck him dead and he fell down. Meanwhile, the Volantine had fled underground, digging further than the Demorgoge could go despite breaking the Earth apart searching for them. Infuriated, the Demogorge rent Gologolthia's body apart, drenching the city in his blood until there was nothing left to desecrate. After the Demorgoge fled, the Volantine returned to their destroyed city. The Mother of Horrors' command to protect his kind wasn't lifted by Gologolthia's death. As his blood had seeped into the ground, stone and destroyed buildings, new towers of flesh rose from the Earth to replace the old structures. Thus, the Volantine survived the Great Culling, thanks to the sacrifice of Gologolthia. ===Later years=== Following the Great Culling, servants of One Above All returned many time to lay waste to the Living City, but every time it rose anew. It eventually came to host all of Vinruviel's children. Aeons later, circa 1600 BC, in Assyria, when Eldest sacked Nineveh and made it her capital, they summoned Gologolthia. The blood and spirit of Gologolthia imbued the stone of the city, watching over its monstrous dwellers. ===Modern Age / New Age of Monsters=== After taking control of the Hulk's persona body, Eldest came to Red Creek, Kentucky, where was set the Mountain Tomb of Udru, and summoned Gologolthia. Thus, Gologolthia became the sanctuary of the monsters in this new Age of Monsters, and her capital. ==Residents== Eldest / Hulk and her army: Udru Jinni Dagaal, the War Devil Skinwalkers Rutlings National Guard David Bridger Formerly: In Nineveh: Eldest / Child-God Charruk As the Living City of the Volantine Choir: Volantine Choir all of the Mother of Horrors' children

gomar.name: Gomar
gomar.origin: Gomar was a member of King Kull's Red Slayers, a group of the finest warriors of Valusia. Gomar and a group of Slayers accompanied Kull and Brule on their journey to find the fabled temple of the Serpent-Men. After being injured in an ambush by the Serpent-Men, Gomar was left behind while Kull led the healthy members of the group towards the temple. While the group was gone, Gomar was tended to and bandaged up. When Kull and company returned, they brought along Thulsa Doom, allegedly a man of Grondar found avenging his fiancé's death in the temple. Gomar immediately recognized Thulsa Doom and attempted to warn Kull, but at that moment, succumbed to his injuries, and fell off his horse to the ground, dead. Brule informed Kull he felt sorcery, and Thulsa Doom, responsible, but Kull dismissed the accusation for the time being.

gomdulla.name: Gomdulla
gomdulla.origin: Years ago, archaeologists discovered the Tomb of Gomdulla, discovering the giant mummy of Gomdulla himself. They placed him on display in an Egyptian museum where he remained for a number of years. One day, two youths were horsing around near the feet of the giant behemoth and accidentally stuck a secret stud in his left foot, releasing the colossus from his slumber. When he awoke, Gomdulla smashed through the museum walls and disappeared for several weeks. Interpol learned of a new cult which had sprung up in Egypt and sent one of its top detectives to put an end to it. Several days later the agent followed a cultist back to Gomdulla's liar and believed his high priest to be in charge of the Cult. The priest demanded more and more money and riches to be piled up in front of the body of Gomdulla. The agent pulled his gun and tried to arrest the priest, it was then that he came to the realization that Gomdulla himself really was alive. Gomdulla swat the gun out of the man's hand and used his power of telekinesis to hurl giant stone at him. Just as things looked bleakest for the agent, the priest himself found the secret stub in the giant's foot and sent him back into a deep slumber. The priest then revealed to the officer that Gomdulla was actually not a pharaoh, but an alien being that had come to Egypt ages ago, he supposedly terrorized people before being trapped within his tomb. The priest also said that he did not wish to be a member of the cult, but became high priest in order to avoid being killed. Years later, the alien mummy was transported to New York City and went out of control once his stub was pressed on. The Fantastic Four quickly arrived to try and fight Gomdulla off, but it was thanks to one punch to the head by Spider-Man that knocked him out. Sometime later, he was among those imprisoned by the Asgardians on Exile Island, but he escaped to Cairo, Egypt. During the Poisons' invasion of Earth, Gomdulla was summoned by Kid Kaiju to aid in Earth's defense along with Goom and Gorgilla.

gomurr.name: Gomurr
gomurr.species: Apprentice to an unnamed sorcerer, Gomurr and his rival Tar were responsible for sealing Cyttorak.
gomurr.origin: A group of monks sought to gain the power of Cyttorak, but were consumed by his destructive power. A tenuous alliance between the Ebon Vein and Gomurr's master led to the two combining their power. They managed to contain the essence in a crystal, which Cyttorak then cursed. Neither trusted the other in safeguarding the crystal, so a temple was chosen to house it. Years later, Cain Marko found the gem and was transformed into the Juggernaut. At some unknown point, Gomurr met Wolverine and the two became friends. Gomurr later migrated to the United States and worked out of a restaurant. When Psylocke was severely injured by Sabretooth, Archangel and Wolverine sought Gommur's help. He quickly determined that the Crimson Dawn would be able to heal her wounds. Doctor Strange noticed a magical disturbance and also arrived to lend his assistance. Tar was now the ruler of the Crimson Dawn and proctor of the Ebon Vein, but he was angry that Gomurr would make such a request. As the two continued their rivalry, Archangel was able to place a portion of Betsy's soul in the Dawn. Gomurr sensed Onslaught placing the Juggernaut into the Crimson Cosmos within the Ruby of Cyttorak. Doctor Strange also arrived at the Xavier Institute, and Gomurr asked Strange to guard the ruby while he entered the dimension. Tar also entered the ruby. Although the demoness Spite was able to trick Marko into confronting Cyttorak, the two sorcerers increased Juggernaut's powers so he could defeat the form Cyttorak took. Juggernaut was sent back to Earth, while Gomurr and Tar took refuge in the Crimson Dawn. When the villain Kuragari killed Tar and abducted Psylocke, Gomurr intervened and rescued her. Tar's spirit named Gomurr as his replacement as Proctor of the Crimson Dawn.

gondor.name: Gondor
gondor.origin: Gondor was a Nazi spy who was active during World War II. By 1942, his operations were operated out of the Gondor Funeral Home located in San Francisco. He would assist Japanese spies in smuggling themselves into the United States. To this end, he had them dispose of the bodies of American soldiers killed in the Pacific Theater and hide in their coffins. After the funerals of the deceased, the Japanese spies would be allowed free to commit acts of sabotage to American defense efforts. This plot was uncovered by the Angel who caught one of these spies attempting to signal the location where a new experiment jet was being developed by starting a fire. Using clues found on the man's body, the Angel followed them back to the Gondor funeral home. Finding the hero snooping around, Gondor had him ejected from the funeral home. Later, when the Angel returned, Gondor and his spies captured the hero and almost succeeded in having him buried alive at the funeral for a fallen soldier. Making enough noise to alert people to free him, the Angel took Gondor down, and he was promptly arrested by military authorities and locked up after he confessed his entire operation. Gondor's fate after the war is unrecorded.

fields.history: Gondor was a Nazi spy who was active during World War II. By 1942, his operations were operated out of the Gondor Funeral Home located in San Francisco. He would assist Japanese spies in smuggling themselves into the United States. To this end, he had them dispose of the bodies of American soldiers killed in the Pacific Theater and hide in their coffins. After the funerals of the deceased, the Japanese spies would be allowed free to commit acts of sabotage to American defense efforts. This plot was uncovered by the Angel who caught one of these spies attempting to signal the location where a new experiment jet was being developed by starting a fire. Using clues found on the man's body, the Angel followed them back to the Gondor funeral home. Finding the hero snooping around, Gondor had him ejected from the funeral home. Later, when the Angel returned, Gondor and his spies captured the hero and almost succeeded in having him buried alive at the funeral for a fallen soldier. Making enough noise to alert people to free him, the Angel took Gondor down, and he was promptly arrested by military authorities and locked up after he confessed his entire operation. Gondor's fate after the war is unrecorded.

gongniu.name: Gongniu
gongniu.origin: Gōngniú was a member of Changdao's crew who was chosen to participate in a drinking challenge against the Invisible Woman. If Susan beat Gōngniú, Changdao would divulge the whereabouts of S.H.I.E.L.D. Agent Aidan Tintreach to them. After nine rounds of whiskey shots, Susan beat Gōngniú as he passed out on the floor in a drunken stupor. But it was revealed that Changdao poisoned Gōngniú's drinks thus killing him while he called on his bodyguards to do the same thing to the women.

gonji.name: Gonji
gonji.origin: thumb|left|125px|Ganji the medicine man Gonji was a medicine man for an unknown Native American tribe that operated out of a southern state that even by the 1941's still remained true to their heritage. His tribe worshiped the wolf, and when they discovered gold on their land and began mining it, the greedy Gonji used local superstition to trick his fellow people into giving him large amounts of gold. To this end, he constructed a convincing wolf costume and posed as the "Wolf-That-Walked-Like-A-Man", attacking his own people until they began providing gold offerings to appease the angry "God". The series of murders attracted the attention of the hero known as the Angel who was not convinced that these killings were the work of a Wolf-Man. Witnessing an offering, the Angel waited until the so-called Wolf-Man came to collect the gold and chased after it. Gonji had trained normal wolves to do his bidding, and they kept the Angel at bay long enough for his fellow tribesmen to capture the Angel and tie him up to a totem pole in sacrifice. When the Wolf-Man attempted to attack the Angel, the hero broke free and fought the "beast" into fleeing back to his cave. There, the Angel beat the Wolf-Man into submission, unmasking him and revealing his true identity and motives. The Angel then turned Gonji over to his people to face justice, and he was summarily executed for his crimes.

gonra.name: Gonra
gonra.origin: thumb|left|350px|Gonra fighting off hordes of Atlanteans before the Temple of the Scorpion|Temple of the Scorpion God ===19,500 BC=== Circa 19,500 BC, one thousand years before the Age of Kull, Gonra of the Sword was an ancient Valusian hero and knight, who had slain thousands of opponents, and bested the greatest warriors of his age. Gonra wielded a sword forged by a priest or a sorcerer, and fired upon by fire of Heaven and by Valusia's Scorpion God himself. He battled hordes of savage Atlanteans when they had decided to destroy Valusia's Scorpion God. That day, Gonra eventually fell to the Atlanteans but saved the Temple of the Scorpion and Valusia as a whole. He was buried in armor in a sepulchre in the woods beside the temple, but his sword was hidden away. ===18,500 BC=== As Count Murom Bora Ballin's daughter Daphna wished to have King Kull love her, she visited the Sorceress, who found out in her Moon-Gem that Kull's favor could be won by finding him a champion that was his equal, as Brule had left Kull and had returned to the Pictish Isles. After she informed Kull, he went with the poet Ridondo to the temple of the Scorpion, retrieved the sword, and finally freed Gonra from his tomb of vines, and defeated him in combat, forcing him to yield before declaring Gonra his equal. The conspirators Meicus and Duarvio intended to plunder the Accursed Room, the throneroom where King Eallal had been murdered by Snake-Men, for riches, despite Meicus' concern about the curse. They taunted a drunken Gonra into opening the door, sealed by Kull who had sank a sword into the lock. Once the Room open, Meicus was frightened to death by the ghost of Eallal, and Gonra slew many Snake-Men before retreating, wounded, to warn Kull, who had already taken the path to the Accursed Room and defeated many Snake-Men himself, including an impersonator of Gonra. Kull decided to cleansed with fire and seal with brick and mortar the Accursed Room. Gonra eventually left and Brule returned, in adventures yet to be recounted.

gonzalo vega.name: Gonzalo Vega
gonzalo vega.origin: Gonzalo "el Martillo" Vega was a mobster active in New York City. He kept his own territory and did not invade his rivals', who included Tony "the Mooch" Muscato and El Brutale, the first of whom reacted accordingly. Vega thought that people in their line of business should not fall into patterns or routines, lest they'd be caught. El Brutale wanted to expand his territory. He allied with Dr. Friday, a Haitian voodoo houngan who used Zombie-like Zhambies with guns and bombs to kill El Brutale's rivals, leaving not witnesses. Vega had only heard that this new enemy was a cult coming from the islands, possibly Caribbean Sea. Vega and Muscato met at the penthouse restaurant Gatti's to discuss the attacks, not knowing that Dr. Friday had sent a Zhambie to kill them there. Moon Knight's would-be sidekick Midnight saved the attendees by pushing the Zhambie out the window before the detonation. Upon learning that his enemies Muscato and Vega, had survived and that there were witnesses who had seen the Zhambies, Brutale was very angry and criticized Friday; but Friday insisted that he had more Zhambies who would kill Brutale's enemies quickly. However, as the situation with superheroes escalated, El Brutale shot Dr. Friday dead, and Friday sent a Zhambie after El Brutale (it is unclear whether El Brutale survived).

goober jones.name: Goober Jones
goober jones.origin: Goober Jones was a friend of Tommy Pidgeon and together with other boys friends of Tommy they wanted to prepare a welcome party for Tommy's Uncle Pete, since he had always been affable and helpful with the boys. Pete had been away on business for a long time, not knowing what kind of work Pete did anyway. Tommy's parents, however, did not agree to the party, telling the boys that Pete would be very tired when he returned and it was better to wait at least a few days. When the limousine that took Pete home arrived the boys were present and noticed that Pete was floating when he got out of the car, so they understood that Pete was an astronaut and had returned from Outer Space and therefore had to readjust to Earth's gravity. Seeing this, the boys and Tommy's parents still organized the welcome party using a trapeze that was in the barn where Pete could lean.

goodfire.name: Goodfire
goodfire.origin: The woman that became Goodfire was one of a trio of hired muscles gathered by the Mad Thinker when he set out to form a new Fantastic Four. Using the equipment owned by Rachna Koul, the Mad Thinker granted himself and the rest of the team powers similar to those of the original Fantastic Four. Goodfire possessed the ability to envelop her entire body on a blue flame, though she wasn't capable of turning off her powers. Calling himself Mister Fantastic, the Mad Thinker took his new Fantastic Four to an alternate universe where the Human Torch and The Thing had become stuck during a multiversal journey in the search for their family. The Mad Thinker intended to eliminate them to consolidate his team since he believed they needed to declutter the void left by the Fantastic Four from its remnants. Despite the fact that both the Human Torch and The Thing were powerless, they managed to hold their own against the Thinker's team. After the Human Torch knocked down Lumen, Goodfire lunged at him. However, Lumen's powers were out of control, causing him to distort the light waves of the environment. She tried to hit The Thing but crashed into a wall instead. After dealing with the remaining members of the Fantastic Four, the Human Torch and The Thing escaped. The duo regained their powers before their second encounter against the new Fantastic Four, and easily defeated the villain and his pretenders. The Human Torch absorbed Goodfire's flame, rendering her temporarily powerless. Before Johnny knocked her out, she thanked him and expressed relief that she could be normal again, and he promised to get her help to permanently undo the mutation. Afterwards, the Human Torch and The Thing returned home, taking the Mad Thinker's team with them.

goodness silva.name: Goodness Silva
goodness silva.species: Human with hereditary animal shapeshifting abilities
goodness silva.origin: ===Origin=== Goodness Silva and her brother Lucky lived in a suburb in Detroit, Michigan with their mother. An ability running in the family, both could turn into animals, a wolf and a two-tailed fox, respectively. ===Great Lakes Avengers=== thumb|left|Good's human form One night, their neighborhood was attacked by several supervillains, secretly hired by councilman Dick Snerd to get rid of high-risk areas. A portion of the Silvas' house was damaged by Firebrand, severely injuring Lucky. Before coming to her brother's aid, Good used her powers to save a neighbour who was being terrorized by the villain Pitchfork. Angered by the councilman's claims, Good located Snard and allegedly threw a glass bottle at him in protest. The GLA's attorney Connie Ferrari looked into Good and temporarily made her part of the Avengers to ensure she wouldn't be prosecuted. They took him hostage, and in a fit of rage, Goodness fatally injured him. When the team found out, they dropped Snerd at a hospital and escaped. Goodness was eventually reunited with Lucky after he escaped from his hospital room, and both decided to leave town. However, Goodness ditched Lucky and returned to Detroit after learning of the GLA's fight against Doctor Nod, helping out the team defeat the villain's Bod Squad.

googam.name: Googam
googam.origin: ===Origin=== Googam is an alien child, the son of Goom from Planet X. One week after Goom's capture and return to his own world, Googam emerged from near where his father had landed, and captured Mark Langley, the man who had brought his father to Earth, and held Mark, his wife Helen, and their son Billy captive while his powers matured and grew. Although Googam's presence at the Langley house was detected by some of the locals, the stories were disbelieved by others. Googam believed that he had reached the height of his power, and prepared to execute the Langleys. Billy claimed that he could beat Googam at a game of tag and led him back into the mountains. Billy then cleverly led Googam straight into a pool of quicksand, where he sank down to his apparent death. Goom and Googam would later be part of the Subterranea forces of the Mole Man in a coordinated assault against every Triple-A baseball stadium, which would fail due to many superheroes intervening across America. During this fight, the father and son aliens would face against the Sub Mariner at Norfolk, Nebraska. Sometime later, he attended a human college for at least some period of time and was popular enough with his classmates to be invited along for a Spring Break trip to Cancun, Mexico. His father tracked him down with the aid of the Angel and the Iceman and brought him home. Goom and Googam were briefly imprisoned along other unidentified aliens at the God Complex in Antarctica, where they fed the inmates on mincemeat. During a potential escape attempt, Goom thought that the snow was radioactive fallout and told the other escapees, including his son, to go back in. ===Monsters Unleashed=== Googam and Goom were two of the handful of Goliathons who were summoned by Kei Kawade using his Inhuman powers to fight on his behalf the Leviathon Tide, which attempted to raze Earth. During the Goliathons' fight against the Leviathons, Googam struggled against an insectoid monster, prompting his father to mock him. Just as Googam was about to be eaten by the creature, Doctor Strange, one of the heroes who were fending off the Leviathon Tide, teleported the monster away and saved Googam's life. Three days later, Googam stormed into Strange's Sanctum Sanctorum, with the intention to kill the sorcerer due to the humiliation that he felt for having the opportunity to defeat the monster allegedly taken from him, causing him to struggle to gain his father's recognition. Strange convinced Googam to accompany him on tracking down the monster, whose location was unknown due to the rudimentary nature of the teleportation spell. Strange and his reluctant ally travelled to Nunavut, Canada, where a magical compass had located the creature. When the insectoid shot Strange's aircraft out of the sky, Googam saved his life. The ensuing fight against the monster was difficult for both Googam and Doctor Strange. Under Strange's directions, Googam led the creature onto a lake covered with thin ice, causing it to sink into the water. As the insectroid struggled to remain afloat, Strange forced it to eat a magical mushroom that shrunk it down and then tied it down with the Bonds of Krottak. Googam accepted Strange's thanks and decided that he no longer needed his father's approval. ===Monster Isle=== Not long afterwards, Googam moved back to Monster Isle and attempted to dethrone the Mole Man and become its new ruler. When the two former members of the Fantastic Four, the Thing and the Human Torch, explored the island, the Mole Man declared that whoever defeated the invaders was to become the new ruler. In an unexpected turn of events, Doctor Doom arrived on the scene and defeated them both. Since he had fulfilled the Mole Man's requirements, the Moloids decided to declare him their new ruler instead. Doom's first order was to have both Googam and the Mole Man sent "deep into the earth." Googam would later be part of a group of monsters that ambushed the Fantastic Four outside a grocery store in Benson, Arizona called Foodtopia, only to be quickly defeated.

goom.name: Goom
goom.origin: ===Invasion of Earth=== The creature called Goom was an alien being from Planet X. Goom had various physical and mental powers as well as advanced technology. An astronomer named Mark Langley used powerful radar waves through a transmitter to look for any other planets in the Solar System. He found a small blue planetoid behind Jupiter, which he named Planet X. The astronomer wanted to see if there was life on that planet, so he tried to communicate with anyone through the transmitter. The alien Goom received the transmission, followed the signal back to Earth and eventually arrived in his spaceship. Goom held Mark and his wife captive and told them they would be needed to help with his conquest of Earth. Goom ordered Mark to tell the people of Earth that he came in peace and would like to speak with the world leaders, or his wife would be destroyed with his neutron beam, which he had used to destroy a mountain before the Langleys' eyes. Mark reluctantly agreed and news of Goom's arrival was on the front page of every newspaper. thumb|left Goom explained to the world leaders to prepare for the new world order and that he would rule mankind. Goom used the power of one of his weapons, wherein he placed one of the world leaders inside a reverse time machine and the man inside reverted backwards into an infant, after which Goom turned him back into an adult. Goom then displayed more of his abilities by lifting an entire city with the power of his mind and creating a force field to protect him from any attacks. While Goom was distracted with his plans for conquest, Mark sent a message back to Planet X and was able to make contact with them. Members of Goom's race arrived on Earth and explained that they were pacifists, not conquerors. They explained that Goom was an outcast of their society. They arrested Goom and took him back to Planet X. Before leaving, however, Goom left the egg of his soon to be born son, Googam, in a nearby cave in an effort to conquer Earth. ===Return to Earth=== Years later, Xemnu the Living Titan created duplicates of five monsters which he used to attack the Hulk. These monsters included Goom, as well as the Blip, Groot, Diablo, and Taboo, all of which were destroyed by the Hulk. The real Goom returned to Earth after his saucer picked up a dating offer by Chili Storm, giving him motivation to start a harem and half-human children to infiltrate Earth society. The goddess of love, Venus, used the Floppy Disk of The Gods to search for a match for Goom, summoning his future wife Princess Shivoor and foiling his plans of conquest. Sometime after, Goom was captured by S.H.I.E.L.D. as a member of the Howling Commandos and contained in Area 13, failing at breaking out. During this time he was used as backup during an assault against Merlin's forces. ===Fatherhood=== Goom and Googam would later be part of the Subterranea forces of Mole Man in a coordinated assault against every Triple-A baseball stadium which would fail due to many superheroes intervening across America. During this fight the father and son aliens would face against the Sub Mariner at Norfolk, Nebraska. Afterward, the two separated with Goom looking for Googam in New York City and causing panic and property damage during his search. Angel and Iceman were able to talk to him and tracked Googam to his college spring break in Cancun, Mexico. Once there, Goom brought Googam back to his saucer while his son was tanning. Goom and Googam were briefly imprisoned along other unidentified aliens at the God Complex in Antarctica where they fed the inmates on mincemeat. During a potential escape attempt, Goom thought that the snow was radioactive fallout and told the other escapees including his son to go back in. Goom later appeared on Monster Isle where fought with Doop, along with several other monsters, when Doop was assigned to help protect the Jean Grey School For Higher Learning. Shortly after, Shadowcat and Magik appeared to look for a mutant girl named Bo. Goom was among the monsters that attacked the three until Magik teleported herself, Shadowcat, and Bo to the Jean Grey School for Higher Learning. Goom, along with Orrgo and a Double-Headed Krackalakassian, were briefly captured by Amadeus and Maddy Cho. ===Monsters Unleashed=== Googam and Goom were two of the handful of Goliathons who were summoned by Kei Kawade using his Inhuman powers to fight on his behalf the Leviathon Tide, which attempted to raze Earth. During the Goliathons' fight against the Leviathons, Googam struggled against an insectoid monster, prompting his father to mock him. Just as Googam was about to be eaten by the creature, Doctor Strange, one of the heroes who were fending off the Leviathon Tide, teleported the monster away and saved Googam's life. During the Poisons' invasion of Earth, Goom was summoned by Kid Kaiju to aid in Earth's defense along with Gorgilla and Gomdulla.

goose brunton.name: Goose Brunton
goose brunton.origin: Goose Brunton was a co-founder of an app called Pufugugu, an app which made food look decayed and low quality. After GRUMBL bought his app, he attended a leadership conference. During said conference, Goose and his friends, Brad and an unnamed woman, invited M.O.D.O.K. to horse golf after he had been humiliated by Austin. During that game, M.O.D.O.K. was able to use Melissa's social skills to undermine the confidence of Goose and his friends and make them desperate for his approval. During the next day at the conference, M.O.D.O.K. grew impatient and opened a portal to Broodworld, letting a group of Ciegrimites into the party. Goose and the other visitors begun partying with the Ciegrimites. Goose died in this party when he broke his spine in a game of Limbo, being tossed onto a pile of dead bodies by the Ciegrimites.

gopher baroque.name: Gopher Baroque
gopher baroque.first_appearance: Peter Porker, The Spectacular Spider-Ham Vol 1 4
gopher baroque.origin: Gopher Baroque was an artist who created a new chemical with his chemistry set, that spilled onto his hand that first turned his paw to stone, which then spread to the rest of his body. Using this he found everything he touched turned to stone and dubbed himself The Grey Gopher. He went to the local part and began turning civilians to stone and planned to use them for his new exhibition. Captain Americat arrived to find where people were disappearing too and was turned to stone by the Gopher himself. Taking him to his studio, he found that Captain Ameri-cat and several overs were his staue slaves and put them to use as putting on a dance show to earn money. At the end of the show, Captain Americat returned to normal as the Gopher realised his power was only temporary and so he was arrested. When all the super-powered beings were captured by the Bee-Yonder for his Secret Furs, this included Paw who was seen being attacked by the Hulk Bunny.

gor kill.name: Gor-Kill
gor kill.origin: A sentient mass of gas crashed into the Krakow Dam near a small coastal town, bonding with the water and formed into a fifty foot water monster. It attacked the nearby town and so the villagers went in search of the monster, which they had dubbed "Gor-Kill" after a local legend. As they were searching for a solid being, found nothing in the water. A drifter named Hans Grubnik realized that the monster was the water, and begged his fellow townspeople not to let the creature make it to the ocean where is could eventually destroy the world due to the amount of water it could absorb. Disbelieving, the villagers were just happy to see Gor-Kill not ransack their town. Grubnik stole a round of dynamite and planted it in a valley and as Gor-Kill stepped over it, Hans set the explosives off. Gor-Kill was dispersed into droplets of water, which were absorbed by the soil.

gor tok.name: Gor-Tok
gor tok.origin: left|thumb Gor-Tok was a prince of a once-great civilization that had been in existence many more years than the "Outer World," the normal world above ground. They were a great warrior tribe who won many wars. There were groups of them throughout the thousands of miles of caverns below ground. As his father was planning to take an army above ground to conquer the people there, a great earthquake destroyed all of the underground civilization and killed all its people save for him. The quake caused him to become mutated by radiation, which made him inhuman in appearance. He believed the surface world was the cause of the destruction of his people and believed it was his duty to avenge teir deaths. The earthquake was caused by Dr. Hunt, who had invented an earthquake machine capable of causing seismic tremors. He first confronted the Iceman and the Beast in a subway tunnel, where he eventually escaped into an underground cavern. He originally had amnesia, but while exploring the caverns he regained his memories. He then sought to use the earthquake machine to destroy the entire Earth, even if it caused him to lose his life in the process. He then confronted the X-Men while using Dr. Hunt's machine. The X-Men succeeded in defeating him as the machine exploded. It seemed at the time that the blast had killed him. The X-Men also believed that Charles Xavier had sacrificed his own life to stop Grotesk. Later, Gor-Tok tried to steal the Cavorite Crystal and with it, destroy the world, thereby exacting his revenge on humanity. Ms. Marvel appeared to battle him but failed in preventing him from obtaining the crystal. Carol Danvers, while out on a date on the beach, discovered Grotesk trying to use a high-intensity laser to activate the crystal's matrix interface. This time Danvers, now in the form of Ms. Marvel, was able to stop Grotesk, appearing to have killed him. However, Grotesk later resurfaced when an alliance comprised of the Subterranean races the Moloids, the Tyrannoids, and the Lava Men burst through the city street, and the Avengers assembled to drive them back underground. Pursuing their opponents, the heroes encountered the Mole Man, Tyrannus, and Grotesk (the latter now the ruler of the Lava Men who had not been transformed by the death of the demon Cha'sa'dra), who revealed that they and their followers were not attacking the surface world, but rather fleeing the attacking Deviants, from whom they had long ago purloined their advanced technology. No sooner did Captain America and the Black Widow go to summon aid than their teammates were besieged by the Deviant leader Brutus and his mutate creations, while their new Subterranean allies retreated to await the battle's outcome. Ultimately, the Avengers were taken captive by their foes. Grotesk held Donald Blake hostage, while his enslaved Lava Men pushed the Living Rock to the surface, where it would explode and devastate the world. Thor arrived to help, but was outnumbered until the Godpack arrived. With their help, Thor defeated Grotesk and destroyed the Living Rock. The energies of the Living Rock had destroyed Grotesk's body, but his disembodied spirit still lived on. The Lava Men were able to transfer said spirit within impenetrable mystical armor. Grotesk and the Lava Men fought against the X-Men in San Francisco. Pixie attempted to teleport through his armor's force field and was almost killed in the process. Nightcrawler noted that his own powers were not mystical in nature. He easily teleported through Grotesk's force field and removed his helmet. With his armor open, the spirit of Grotesk dissipated.

goran maledicta.name: Goran Maledicta
goran maledicta.origin: Goran was one of the guardian of the sacred Terrigen Cavern. After Quicksilver managed to infiltrate the Cavern and expose himself to the Terrigen Mist (in order to restore his powers after the M-Day), and despite having used his newfound time-travel powers to evade detection, Goran was assigned to "escort" him at any times he left his apartment. ===Death=== Goran was present when Quicksilver took the stolen Terrigen Crystals (who would be stolen only eleven days later) to his daughter Luna. Once in Luna's room, away from Goran's sight, Lockjaw would teleport them away to Earth. Eleven days later, allied with a future duplicate of himself, Quicksilver infiltrated the Cavern once again. Despite Quicksilver ally and Genetic Council member Videmus' attempt to take him away from the scene, Goran felt that something was wrong, and while Quicksilver future-self went to collect Terrigen Crystals, Goran discovered present Quicksilver, who accidently killed him while trying to defend himself (before returning eleven days earlier with the stolen crystals). After the other Maledicta siblings went to Black Bolt as ordered by Videmus, the council member asked them to arrest him for high treason: He led the Maledicta and the Royals to Goran's body, while other Maledicta bursted on the scene to inform them of the stealing of the Crystals.

gorax.name: Gorax
gorax.first_appearance: The Age of the Sentry Vol 1 1
gorax.origin: Gorax's brain was removed and ended up in the collection of Cranio through unknown means. It was retrieved by the Sentry and given to Dr. Hugo Cornelius. The doctor placed the brain in his newly discovered "living gelatin" which allowed Gorax to regrow his body. He was immediately attacked by the Sentry, but Gorax absorbed some of his life force, knocking him out. Gorax then sought vengeance against Cranio but was immediately knocked out by the Sentry when he found Cranio, knocking the brain out of the gelatin.

gordon.origin: The Great King Kalden exiled Gordon and Snarkle through a portal two-thousand years ago. The Inhuman Iso discovered schematics for the portal within New Attilan, and with a bit of help from Flint, eventually "fixed" the Inhuman tech, allowing them to reopen the portal. Snarkle then seized Flint, and commanded Gordon to grab Iso, but Gordon had other plans, helping Iso to close the portal so that he remained in exile, this time alone.

gordon allsworth.name: Gordon Allsworth
gordon allsworth.origin: Gordon Allsworth developed an interest in mythology during his youth, particularly the legends of Hercules, which he preferred to the comic books read by his classmates. As an adult, he became a television host and director, eventually working on The New Labors of Hercules, a program documenting Hercules' attempts to recreate his legendary labors in the modern world. Gordon accompanied Hercules and his crew on several of these adventures, including encounters with Ka-Zar, Shanna, HYDRA, Attuma, the Red Skull, the Abomination and Doctor Doom. Although he initially treated Hercules' exploits primarily as television entertainment and was willing to portray some of them as little more than lucky successes for the sake of ratings, Gordon's attitude changed after learning about Hercules' ancient murder of his wife and children and witnessing his confrontation with their spirits in Hades. Gordon later became the host of Monsters, Myths and Marvels, an investigative program devoted to challenging popular stories concerning the superhuman community. In one episode, he attempted to demonstrate that Galactus' arrival on Earth and subsequent defeat by the Fantastic Four had been an elaborate hoax. He interviewed several people in support of his theory, although most superheroes refused to cooperate with him. While producing an episode about the Wendigo near Lac Saint-Jean, Canada, Gordon and cameraman Jimmy witnessed their reenactment turn into a real-life attack when an actual Wendigo killed several members of the crew. Gordon and Jimmy survived after Wolverine intervened, and after being questioned by the authorities, they promptly left the country.

fields.notes: The appearance of Gordon Brown got considerable attention from the press, contrasting the comic's heroic portrayal with the PM's current poor standing with the voting public. Cornell said "I'm quite a fan of Gordon Brown. I'm pleased we've given him a PR boost on both sides of the Atlantic and around the world. I feel quite sorry for him, so I'm glad I've contributed a bit."
